reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was worth seeing... sort of. Having been there, I wouldn't go back. Let me start with the pros. The drive there is scenic and if you like driving along the mountains on serpentine roads, then you'll enjoy the drive. The beach is clean and the water is calm and clear. It is great for kids. As for pros, that's it. Now the cons. Depending on where you're coming from, it can be a long drive. From Rethimnos, it took us 2.5 hours. Parking costs 5€ unless you're early and the closer parking lot is 3€. There are official looking people directing you to lots. They just work for each lot. The walk down to the beach takes 15 minutes to walk over rough terrain. If you want an umbrella and 2 chairs, it costs 20€. If you want more than coffee you have to hike back up. Elafonisi is also known as the pink beach. The pictures online don't reflect reality. There is pink sand but only where the water washes on the sand - thin band.  The rest of the sand is the run of the mill beach sand. It is also very busy and crowded. We went on a Sunday so perhaps it isn't as busy on a weekday but most of the people were tourists anyway. If you're looking for a beach, there are just as nice beaches throughout Crete and with better amenities. I'm glad I saw it, but having seen it, I wouldn't return.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Elafonissi Beach is a paradise with pink sand and clear turquoise waters. It’s perfect for relaxing, swimming, and exploring the shallow lagoon. Despite its popularity, it wasn’t overcrowded. The beach has sunbeds, umbrellas, and snack bars. The scenic drive to get there adds to the experience. A must-visit in Crete!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: POOR Customer Service! NOT WORTH VISITING!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worst experience with this paid beach location I've ever had! i just had a family vacation in Crete and heard about this pink (not pink!!) sandy beach. We were very disappointed about this tourtist attraction for the follwing reasons: 1. bad winding and rough road from the gate to the beach, not suitable for elderly and those who have bad knees. It takes about 10min to walk from the gate to the beach. 2. Not enough beach umbrellas and chairs even we are willing to pay! And yet most of the trees are blocked and not allowed to use. Tourists have to rest under shaded tree they can find on the island.3. But WORST OF ALL is the attitude of people guarding this island! Because most of the trees are blocked, we had a hard time to find shaded areas we we could rest and enjoy the beach.  There was a woman who worked there who was very rude and impolite. Instead of helping or telling us which part on the island we can go to find trees for camping, she keeps yelling chasing tourists away from the trees that were blocked. Her behaviour by all means is reflecting POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE!I would not come here again. NOT RECOMMENDED!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Funny!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We started from Chania to go!!! The road dangerous in several places with narrow passages. We arrived at 9:00 in the morning. We parked in a huge parking lot and from there you go down a dirt road every ten minutes on foot... Many had babysitters who had to go down this messy road. Especially in the uptake after it is straight discomfort!! Sleeves not for sample. We asked for a price and they told us 30€ but you didn't play to find it until the sun reigned. There were some gaps that they had reserve... Your umbrella does not play to manage to attach as there is a lot of air and do not sit!!! When we left at 12:00 at noon it played to have over 2,000 people!!! Nice beach to get wet to take a swim and leave!!!Good luck!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Pink Sands and Crystal Clear Waters
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Elafonissi Beach is a paradise! The pink sand and turquoise waters are breathtaking. It's perfect for swimming and relaxing. The beach can get crowded, so arrive early. Facilities are basic, but the natural beauty more than makes up for it. A must-visit in Crete!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Return after 15 years ...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Elafonissi a very beautiful beach, still natural. The beach was pink..now after years of tourist passages,,which took away shells....so much pink is not.  Very nice water and is particular .Sicuramente recommended excursion .Unica thing, we had already been 15 years ago .. unfortunately now it is much more exploited at the level of tourist groups .. so it is not a deserted beach . Even there sunbeds and umbrellas. But not for everyone .. just for those who arrive early .. Anyway it is worth seeing. Take a bath.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonsi July 2024
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I must say that the beach was very beautiful and the sea looked like a swimming pool, but it was very crowded and taking a parasol was like winning the lottery. It is considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Crete and for this I expected it but I was not very enthusiastic. The sand is pink only in some places.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disability experience at Elofonisi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was hesitant to visit elofonisi beach as an ambulatory wheel chair user. The walk down the dirt road seemed daunting when researching the beach before hand. When my husband and I parked in the lot above the dirt road to enter the beach , a parking attendant noticed my wheelchair and guided us to the gate where we were then able to drive the 15 minute walk and access the beach from a closer area. There are board walks to get you to the actual sand, some areas are in rough condition , but with assistance I was able to get right to the umbrella area. The umbrellas are much closer to the water than I expected which was another bonus. Just wanted to share my experience as others may be in a similar situation , that some accommodations are possible to make the experience more accessible!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful site without tourists 😏
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, one of the most beautiful ridge. Trip Tip in summer go early, around 9am there until noon because after the world arrive in packages and necessarily loses its charm. Victim of overtourism in the afternoon. Sunbed 20 euros and parking 5 euros.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise on earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lord gave us Heaven on earth. I Love Greece 💙🫶🏻... 20€ for a full day of umbrella and sunbeds in front of eternity ..? What more do you want. Arriving Max at 9:00 am is mandatory if you do not want to lie on the ground. With 1.30h drive from Chania. Road with some curves but asphalted and quiet to do. Organized parking 200m from paradise at 3/5€. Mandatory stop for those coming to Crete 😍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth only for your some pic all things considered
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Overrated. Tourists have stolen pink pieces of shells.Overpriced sun beds.Parking business owners try guide you to their parking places but you can find parking much closer if you dont follow their guide.Worth of your some pic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic place! There is good parking, cafes and toilets.  Quite a lot of people in July, but there is enough space for everyone :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach with pitfalls !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Attention when choosing a parking space. Right at the beginning are several men who have allocated us a parking space at the end of the world (although you could still have driven 800m). The paid parking fee of 5€ is then only valid in this parking lot and must be paid again when repackaging further forward. Since they are ‘different companies’.The beach itself is beautiful but also very touristy (but you can expect that). For loungers you should be early;)Unfortunately, we could later watch two men stealing on the beach (around evening). So don't take valuables to the beach.Kiosk and toilet tip top

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fine, but far to go
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely place but a bit far to walk from the parking lot (which was organized by p-guards) and incredibly lots of people. Very shallow water, must go far and long to get to waist plus. But definitely an experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very, very beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach on the island. The strip of sand that is created between the outcropping rocks creates a shallow lagoon with truly crystal clear water. Before choosing the day of the visit to the beach it is always better to consult the weather, with the strong wind (often present) is less pleasant but still beautiful. Near the beach there are paid parking lots (5 euros), do not be convinced by the caretakers (parking vendors) to park in the first parking lots you meet, it is always better to check for yourself if the one closest to the beach is complete (the cost is the same for everyone). Also in this resort as on other beaches there are umbrellas and sun loungers for a fee and some bars offering food and drinks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach with indescribable colors You have to arrive very early to find a free cot we arrived at 8:30 and we had no problems Too bad the crowding especially in the free part The price is worth the wonder of the place 30 euros 2 sunbeds and umbrella For the disabled you can arrive by car in front of the beach Beach not to be missed

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Caribbean in Crete
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach... priceless sea... the top of Crete for me... on the way back Recommendation stopping by Statos tavern on the way as soon as you glimpse the gorge by car to return home...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Many people but unique place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Elafonisi is a beautiful and unique beach that they are trying to preserve from the crowds. so the parking has been set back about 500 m from the beach. do not stop at the first parking lots, the last one before the bar is huge and costs only 5 euros per day. then the descent is easy even for children, you get to the beach with umbrellas , two bars, the bathroom (1 euro) and the shower (free). Respect the rules, throw the waste in the many bins and do not make noise. The wind can be strong so you will need the beach umbrella, you will find it free only if you arrive by 9.30 (but already at 14 some leave). 20 euros in July umbrella and two sunbeds. of course this is the busiest part and the peak of crowds you have between 11 and 16. after it returns to be livable and is a paradise. if you can walk to the end of the islet in front there are benches and a church. the colors of the sea are beautiful change depending on where you are and the passing of the day and the direction of the wind. when we were there the wind was 20 knots in the middle of the day and is unbearable but if you go to the left there are more sheltered coves (I wrapped myself in the towel and slept).  We loved it, it's worth the wake up call at dawn, expect big crowds (it's a bit like going to Mont Saint Michel and then complaining).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise early in the morning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Site remarkable for its landscapes, white sand colored red in places, crystal clear water... we take full eyes🤩 arriving between 8 and 9am.Too bad that from 11am the place is overcrowded by tourists who arrive by hordes (bcp bus,cars which explains the size of mandatory parking on arrival)The site then changes and its vision is no longer so idyllic...To do again out of summer season!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ok beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach with lots of wind but extremely many people. Va long to walk from the parking lot which also costs 5 euros. Had expected pink beach but that I saw nothing to.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most beautiful beach I've ever went to. Long beach with pink sand and turqouise shallow water. There are a lot of tourists, but since it's such a long beach it doesn't feel overcrowded at all. There are sunbeds, but if you would like to rent one you should come earlier in the morning. This beach is a must visit if you come to Crete!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's just a shame, I've known the beach for decades, no sign of pink sand. Just mass tourism.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a shame, I have known the beach for decades and was always thrilled. Now I have to say just creepy I was there in June 2023 and immediately went again funfair in the Ruhr area is empty against it! Tried again in April 2024, although empty, there was hardly any trace of the Pink Sand. It is also no wonder as tourists have no respect for nature! Even fenced areas are settled to sunbathe there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but world!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach crystal clear water, some pink sand by the sea.Lots of deckchair a little expensive (20 euros)Many people because beach very touristy but which remains accessible.Very large parking upstream of the beach.Allow 10-15min walk accessible to all

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonisis
reviewsWithKeywords.text: From a naturalistic point of view nothing to say, the sea is beautiful... clear water, but too crowded .. at 10 there was no longer room, and you risk finding people 1 MT away... then pink there is nothing more... to be quieter I suggest to go a little 'beyond the main beach... and Recommendation also to bring an umbrella and lots of water ..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing and sad
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 15 years ago it was a beautiful beach.  Today is a disaster.  Almost no pink sand , overcrowded beach ..... a lot of km for not much in the end . The Greek state should do qqch to preserve this place before it is too late.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heavenly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning scenery. We arrived by ten and were able to rent umbrella and sunbeds. In the late morning many people arrived but the beach is so wide that it is not affected. Da vedere!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but for a while!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A different beach. Nice waters if you walk and pass the crowd. Pink sand you ⁇  do not see in the degree of photos circulating on the internet. Now that time you go there is people, as everyone reads the reviews that say to go in the morning! Now the route is okay is not ideal, but it's rough. As soon as you arrive you stop "various" telling you that below there is no parking space, you come in and park 5€ for the whole day. Walking you realize that you were "drunk" and that there were other parking spaces closer at the same cost (and more are being built). It has a mini market where you can buy various items. Below you will see they sell and umbrellas of sea, don't take, from so much air it doesn't stand. So get ready for enough sunscreen, hat and water. It has little walk to reach the beach, not of great difficulty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is within a protected nature reserve, the colors are wonderful, especially in the middle hours of the day, when the sun is high, the shallow waters form several islets between or which you walk in water of breathtaking beauty.It is very busy but there are many parking lots (5€ per day) about a kilometer from the beach. To get there you take a dirt road that is definitely feasible for those who can walk (to avoid if with strollers or prams and maybe in the hottest hours).There are some sun loungers and bars but most of the beach is not equipped to preserve its beauty. Windy, the umbrellas do not hold, you should go there early in the morning or after 16 when the crowd begins to drop.The sand is pink but it is not Barbie beach, pink are shades between the white sand, visible especially on the shore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique natural phenomenon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible place, magic! He's walking! You get the necessary things, the umbrella doesn't stand up, you sit a little away! Unless you get sunbeds 20 €! It's not a beach for bathing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful piece of paradise!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach and lagoon with pristine water, and long stretches of sandy shoreline. The drive down is a picturesque one with deep valleys and huge olive groves. Be sure to be there before 9am otherwise bring your own umbrella as the limited amount available will be taken.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but.....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with pool style sea, but the path to do on foot is not easy and two adults from other groups fell ruinously on the stones. I add the problem that starting from Kissamos with organized tour when we arrived there was no longer an umbrella available and for survival two of us redid the uphill journey to go buy two umbrellas in the bazaars near the parking lots. They should warn of the journey ahead and the possibility of not finding a place under umbrellas, that with the sun sinking you risk ending up in the emergency room. Last thing you have to hope the wind is not strong, the sand is worse than whippings and you go home breaded

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Crowded of course but still worth a visit. Very beautiful, very hot so bring some sort of shade with you ( very limited amount of sunbeds with shade available. Some walk to beach from parking lot, super clear and warm water, some pink on the waterline left. Super smooth sand

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful but impractical
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beach very beautiful from a naturalistic point of view but completely impractical, strong wind everywhere, areas of shadows practically non-existent, very crowded. It's worth it for a bath but not for the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach with pink sand and lots of shallow wading areas.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Elafonissi Beach is widely known as "the pink beach" because of its pink sand.  It is a beautiful beach and would be perfect for families with small kids, as the water in most areas ranges from ankle- to waist-deep (on an adult).  There can get to be a lot of people, but the beach is large enough to handle it without feeling crowded in most areas.While the beach does have pink sand - thanks to the ground-up shells of local shellfish - it is not the flamingo pink that you may see in the pictures for the tour companies.  It's still a beautiful beach, but if you're looking for knock-your-socks-off pink, you will be disappointed.The drive there can be a bit... interesting.  If you're not comfortable driving on narrow mountain roads with the occasional switchback and a couple of blind corners, you may want to take a bus tour to get there.  Personally, I'm a control freak so I'd rather be driving than sitting up high in a bus and looking down at all that, but that's just me.The day we went was VERY hot by late morning, and VERY windy.  They offer sunbeds with umbrellas for rent, but there is a limited number available.  On the advice of a friend, we purchased a small beach umbrella for 15 Euros before we arrived and it worked perfectly.  You do want to make sure you push it pretty far into the sand - we saw a few blowing across the beach.  But it is worth it - there is not a lick of shade anywhere on the beach.Speaking of advice - passing along advice from a previous review.  If you arrive by car, park in the 3rd parking area (there is a huge sign above it that says "Mega Park" or something like that).  You can't go further - the road is blocked right after this lot.  It is only 5 Euros to park for the day and you pay when you leave.  There is plenty of parking here, and it's a shorter walk than the other lots.There is a decent walk down to the beach, so you'll want to stay for a bit to make it worthwhile.  The water is amazingly clear and refreshing on a hot day.  We found one of the few sheltered areas next to a hill near the snack bar, planted our umbrella, then went for a bit of a walk and a swim.  We hung out under our handy umbrella a bit for a break from the sun and a quick snack, then went back out to cool off for that walk back up to the car.Also - if you have the chance, stop by the Cave of Agia Sofia afterwards.  Again, a good climb, but it's an amazing cave with religious icons, pigeons, and it's free!  There's also a great little taverna to enjoy a quick break on the way back down.In all - as with most tourist spots, reasonable expectations help to avoid disappointments.  There is pink sand, but it's not glowing pink; it's a great beach for families or just to walk around, but it's windy and very hot in the summertime.  Still definitely worth the trip if you have an open day in your itinerary.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We hired a taxi service to take us from Chania to this beautiful beach. We arrived early, so it was perfect, but by the time we left, it was really crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach but watch the car parking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach but gets busy. Go early if possible, especially if you want to take photos. Very very beautiful though!My one tip is if you’re driving, don’t fall for the car park scam. As you drive in you’ll see various people in hi vis, looking very official, flagging you into car parks, some of them quite a walk from the beach. Just drive by (they’ll try to stop you) and go to the bottom car park by the modern looking restaurant which often has spaces. If not you can always drive back up to the more empty ones.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but VERY touristy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very beautiful, the water is crystal clear. For pink sand, I think we should preserve this site by limiting access. Too many people everywhere.It will cost you 5€ of parking for the day.  Lots of wind, and no shade.Nevertheless the site is worth a visit. This lagoon at the foot of the mountain is really beautiful. It must be much nicer in September or October.The restaurant before the car parks is quite affordable in terms of Award, and the view from the terrace is really beautiful.If you come from the north of the island (Chania, Kissamos), the mountain road is also worth a visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's not pink, unserviced
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely in services, more than a km away between brush rocks and sun. Absolutely not pink, people sick on the way back, a van for emergency pay toilets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crystal Waters and a must see natural wonder
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are going to Crete then this is a must. Getting there is not a breeze though as the island is well known for its scary as hell to drive mountainous cliff edge roads. We arrived around 11am expecting it to be packed but any earlier and we might not have had clear roads the entire way. Car parking is €5 which is really cheap. There are a few tacky seaside shops but do stick up ok water. Don’t take little kids. There is zero shade and you won’t get pushchairs down there and you’ll likely end up carrying them which it’s too unsteady and hot to do. Don’t go if you have limited mobility, it’s a place of nature so the Greek have not meddled with it and not should they. There’s a few sun beds and umbrellas at €20 a pair of beds otherwise it’s your beach towel. Water is stunning. Do walk across to Elafonisi island for the pinkest sand and clearest waters (and fewer people). Ignore the negative reviews, this is a 10/10 must see and visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonissi beautiful, wild between nature and colors!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view of this beach is absolutely spectacular. A sea of colors, pink sand and crystal clear sea, shallow waters. Ideal for long and relaxing walks. The beach is huge, beautiful and wild! There are paid car parks for those who come by car. Leaving the car you have to take a walk of about 900 meters on foot. So you can reach small well-served establishments with umbrellas and street for 20 euros, bars and toilets for a fee (1 euro), showers with room temperature water (not for a fee). Elafonissi is a corner of paradise to see and experience for those who come on holiday to Crete. Absolutely fantastic beach 🏖️!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: To flee in high season
reviewsWithKeywords.text: To flee in high season! Far too many people! parking is 5€ for the day cheap but not reported. Pink sand no longer exists because too many visits! We should preserve this site absolutely!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very pretty beach with a tinge of pink sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very pretty beach and worth the visit, however be aware it can get vey windy and the sand only has a slight tinge of pink to it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty, but preferred Falassarna
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is very pretty, but so not worth it. It’s packed with people, there are gale-force winds, and it’s tricky to find a spot to lay your towel out. The water in the lagoon is very instagrammable, but it’s too shallow to really swim (unless you’ve got kids). The pink sand is also not like in the pictures. It’s mostly white sand with pink patches, which are beautiful, but you can see pink patches at Falassarna beach, and it’s a much better, bigger beach. People were arriving in droves by 10 am, and we ended up leaving after just under an hour. To windy and crowded to really enjoy. And it’s hard to get good IG pics because of the crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A really beautiful sea that is very reminiscent of the Sardinian sea, the sand is really pink, shallow and it is very pleasant to walk and cool down. Everything is so big that there were a lot of people but in the end you do not even notice. True that you have to arrive early in the morning, both if you want to take an umbrella (we arrived at 10 am and it was all full) and if you want to find a place near the trees where you can take advantage of the shade every now and then (Recommendation to the right of the establishment that we find ourselves in front of just arrived at the beach, there are trees that give shelter). The day was pleasantly breezy and therefore for me the best beach visited in this holiday

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not worth the visit. Too crowded and not pink.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I am so glad we read the some of the reviews before we travelled so we were not expecting much.It is indeed very overrated. Not a pink beach at all. Little sections near the shoreline have some pink sand otherwise it's just sand with a hint of pink. It's definitely not one of the best beaches, it's just a beach with shallow nice crystal clear water but packed with a few hundred people. I've been to many better sandy beaches with great views and a lot less people.We arrived early as recommended by other reviews, 9am. We arrived by car and ignored the first few car parks, as recommended and parked at the closest to the beach. It's 5 euros for the day. We were thankful we parked at the nearest one on the walk back to the car from the beach because of the heat it felt like a 29 minute walk.By 9am nearly all of the sunbeds were taken and within an hour or so the sunbeds were gone and also nearly every stretch of sand was taken. (20 euros for 2 sunbeds / 30 euros for 4 sunbeds)We watched holidaymakers trying to keep their umbrellas up in the wind with a few blowing away and nearly causing serious damage. We were thankful we had sunbeds and an umbrella. You really need some kind of shade as the sun is unrelenting.Toilets are 1 euro to use and guess what there were no queues for it. I guess the warm crystal clear water became a free toilet for many!I think that if you have absolutely nothing else to do and I mean absolutely nothing else ....and you want to spend some time with a few hundred people on a beach then make the long journey to this beach....otherwise read the reviews....you are not missing out on anything.... and give it a miss and find somewhere more worthy of spending your day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but not like the videos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So whilst staying in Kalyves we booked a trip to Elafonisi beach . After getting picked up and grabbing everyone else from the local area . We stopped for breakfast at a local honey place on the way for breakfast . Beautiful.Then the haul through the mountains, very tight for a coach but the driver knew how to drive.We got to elafonisi and it looked amazing. After a ten minute trek to the beach we found that it was absolutely packed ( the videos online are took late afternoon after all the tourists leave ) .Beautiful place and yes glimpses of pink but not like the pictures online where they’ve been enhanced with bright pink . Had the three hours there and enjoyed the scenery and paddling as it doesn’t get very deep . On the return journey we stopped at a taverna in the mountains and tried a local dish which was absolutely stunning. A very long day but worth it to say we had been .The diver and the tour guide were absolutely amazing and told us some great stories and history of the region .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The road is long and full of curves but you get close, 5 minutes walk from the beach. Huge and equipped beach. Recommendation to arrive early to enjoy the place before the masses arrive. Mass that however in July is not perceived because the place is really great. Immense. You walk a lot and the water always comes to the calf. Incredible colors and lovely water walk. Paradise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice place to swim especially when crossing a lagoon, go early in the morning to avoid the crowds. Pink color is not very visible but water clarity yes true to descriptionIt is a beach to make.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is really wonderful. Nearby there are ample parking lots. You have to walk a bit (no big deal) and before your eyes a real wonder opens. In the most sheltered part from the wind, there is a bathing establishment and small bar with food and drink (and also some confusion!). Continuing and exploring on foot, there are places where the water forms natural pools: there are fewer people and it is truly a paradise. A spectacle: impossible to resist the temptation to take very long baths. If the wind allows, you can bring and plant your own umbrella. Crystal clear water. Wonderful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A little paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the excursions to do absolutely Beach with coves and beautiful sea Equipped with umbrellas, (not many) better arrive early to find a place and toilet Pink sand in some areas.Unfortunately the photos do not do justice to this little paradise on earth

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonissi to fail
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good morning, I want to tell you what the elafonissi experience is really like.Then just to start the beach is not pink because they stole it all, then, to reach the beach from the parking lot you have to walk at least 1 km and a half under the sun and it's full of stones and there's no real path, you also risk falling between the stones and on the way back we found a strong wind so as to raise the sand and make it fall on us like so many knives, never lived such a bad experience in all my life.Then, if you want an umbrella with 2 sunbeds, according to them you have to go very early or at 14:00 or 17:00, because the places are few and 'absolutely not true that they are organized, if you want to pay by card you have to take a further walk to the bar, as well as if you want to get water.The problem (another ) is that if you don't have an umbrella then you have to put yourself in the shade and you have to think about it in the sense that if you have low blood pressure or are pregnant they don't give a damn, so the service sucks doubly because you are forced to find shade under trees where the Greeks don't even want you to go in fact they are fenced, but cmq was full of desperate people.As for the sea and 'definitely beautiful but the water and' shallow, you can find the same are with a little higher water and with a service 100 times better in falasarna.Elafonissi 1 umbrella and 2 sunbeds 20 euro.Falasarna 30, but those extra 10 euros are all earned they even bring you lunch under the umbrella.Greetings to all Italians.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rimini in mid-August
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach, nice view, in a very nice area of Crete. Being the most famous beach in Crete is worth a star for me.Perché ? Because when you arrive they charge you 5 euros for parking. I walk 10-15 minutes to get to the beach and this is fine because so the natural park remains intact. But once you get to the beach it seems to be in Rimini or riccione on August 15. Already when you arrived, we were about 10.15, lookouts already in snake of people walking towards the beach. Once down you see the delirium. People everywhere, both on the beach and in the sea. If you want to come and find tranquility here for sure you will not find it. A real shame about the place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Place on the side
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Parking: 5€ all parking so take the nearest one and don’t be fooled by the folders we can mistake for placiders Location: it’s beautiful yes but it’s really windy and we haven’t seen pink sand. There are people but we know that in the summer, there is still a lot of room not to be stuck to people. Water: very pleasant temperature, we walk away (ideal for children)What really ruined our experience was the wind, the pebbles in the water, the little shade and not seeing the pink sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful few umbrellas lots of crowds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice but with few umbrellas, we arrived at 10:00 and it was already sold out. We parked at the last parking lot paying 5€. Then we left because so many people kept coming

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach alayaa to there
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On July 24, we started to go to this famous beach!!!!We woke up from 8 a.m. and after driving on a miserable and dangerous road we arrived.They didn't let us go down to the last parking lot and they forced us to park high.After walking a path we reached low to the beach where although it was 10 a.m. you could not sit because of the air but because of the clay. You couldn't put an umbrella.The air took it.At the return we had an obstacle the heat but the hills.... very beautiful beach alayaa.....it is for you to go see it and go...also....classic as in all of Crete....all for the profit....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach but really too crowded, will be that we arrived around 10.30, uncomfortable walk to reach it obligatorily feet if you have the stroller.To fully enjoy it it would be advisable to reach it around 8-9 am.We arrived at that time did not find sunbeds available and so we took advantage of the shade of the large cedars near the beach to stay a little protected.Ideal for children as the water is really shallow and degrading so that to take a bath you have to go a little offshore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spiaggia meravigliosa!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Comfortable beach, easily accessible with short walk and flat. White sand with pink shades and crystal clear water. The water is very shallow on the shore and rises gradually. You have to arrive by 9.30/10.00 to find umbrellas and sunbeds, because there are not many. Instead there is plenty of space for free beach. Great beach, must see!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What to do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful water, only catch he makes to be there very early to have a deckchair Watch out for the folders of the front car parks who try to get you into theirs, while further there is plenty of room 5 € per seat

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Crowded & More like a Lagoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to a lot of other beaches in Crete and this one was by far the most overrated. The parking was a bit chaotic and you had to convince a man to open a gate into the beach. The beach itself was very overcrowded and filled with trash near the water. We got there around 10:15 and were able to get the last sunbeds they had. The food was abysmal compared to standards around Crete. I think the biggest downside of this beach is that it is way too crowded and does not have any waves. It’s not much of a beach and more like a lagoon. The water is warm enough for swimming. The pink sand was nice but not much like the photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach for surfing and posing... It is a must on the island but as a beach it has much better... a lot of walking......

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dante's group
reviewsWithKeywords.text: But the translation is perhaps...nightmare beach...a long way to go under the scorching sun, despite the countless whyggi down near the beach.Instead they make you park high on buses. Rivers of people going down and up, it's like a Dante ring.Trees that could make a little shade, sadistically are fenced so you don't go.Finally a strong wind that grinds you with sand. an ordeal that does not compensate for the trip

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach was ok, very few umbrellas or places for any shade or a break from the heat. We got there at 1100 and not a thing left. Thousands of people already before noon. Not really pink sand, at least when we were there - a little bit at the waters edge. Lots of parking - if you come before noon ignore the first few lots, there’s a big parking lot closer to the beach, as well as a few stores, cafes, washrooms. Lots of other beautiful beaches easier to get to and much less crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is not worth visiting during peak summer season as there are thousands of people at the same time on the beach. It is crowded and if you arrive after 10 in the morning there is no way to get into sunshade .We traveled al the way from Heraklion ( by car) and we do not recommend the hassle ! The water looks and feels good.To be honest, it is overrated and too crowded ! Stop advertising the pink sand as there are limited time frames where it is visible.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointment!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Is Elafonisi really one of the best beaches in Crete? The answer is ambiguous. The distance from Chania you will spend in the car is definitely not worth it for this beach! The beach is boasted by all the tourist guides, so prepare for the globe. Prepare also for walking from the parking lot to the beach. The beach itself is rather indifferent, drowned in the world and you need to be there early to secure sunbeds... What about the pink sand? It is scattered here and there and definitely not as intense in color as in the photos you will see on the Internet!Prefer one of the adjacent coves, next to the main beach with the island if you want to find somewhere to sit and of course take a bath! In conclusion, beautiful beach but drowned in the world, especially in the summer! Surely there are better beaches in the area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach in the world!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing views, by far the most beautiful beach we’ve ever been to, if not in the world. Great snorkelling water, as there’s rocks with many species of fish to see. The water is clear and shallow enough to wade out and safe for both kids and non swimmers. The only negative is that’s it’s over crowded as there’s hundreds of people, however you’ll not be disappointed by the views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A wonderful trip to Elafonisi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A wonderful trip, with a responsible, noble and pleasant guide, Vasilis and with an exciting tour by Mr. Dimitris, whom I consider the best guide I have met so far and who made me know the history of my own place more deeply!!A big thank you for such friendly, familiar, warm and human escort and tour that made this excursion to Elafonisi an unforgettable experience!!Goodbye!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and paradisiacal landscape but too touristy for my taste. I recommend arriving very early in the morning to enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't go.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I leave a negative review as highly overrated compared to many beautiful coves of clay. First of all we arrive and they signal us to park at that point, when later there was a huge parking accessible for a fee always at the same price: five euros. After that we arrive after one km, the beach was crowded and full of families with screaming children (we went to coves even on the weekend where we and the goats were). Not bad water but the problem was the very strong wind that lifted the sand. You couldn't even eat sand coming in and stinging you everywhere. Not even a shaded area to shelter from wind and sun. Absolutely not going there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful water too bad the wind
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sea, shame the wind so strong that it pulled up the sand.Baths and showers for a fee a 1 euro xò the bar offered fairly low prices x a sea place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's worth being there for sure.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach! The water is clean, the sand isn't as pink as the Internet photo, but it's still beautiful very. There are places with puddles for children where the water is very shallow and warm. Sunbeds are 20€ for 2 pcs, on the beach cafe with food (pizza, baguette, burger and snacks) drinks and ice cream. Before going down to the beach cafe, restaurant and shops with food and inflatable toys, large parking (5€ day), the possibility to rent a room and tp in the shop drinks and food are of course cheaper than on the beach. It is better to arrive in advance, because sunbeds and places under umbrellas are dismantled very quickly. Toilet on the beach 1€.It was easy and easy from Chania, good road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not worth the hype!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has lots of hype surrounding it. I was rather disappointed!No one tells you that's it's a 20min from the car park down a gravel and rocky path. Not for those with limited mobility or young child. Seen families struggle with prams.Once at the beach it had hundreds and hundreds of people on it which kinda takes away the shine of this beach.2 Sunbeds with a parasol and €20! To use the toilet it's €1! Food and drink was OK in price.The tour we took advised us to buy a parasol from the shop at the car park. Some people did but it was a waste of time as the wind just blew them inside out.You can walk across the water to the little island and this is where we seen the most pink sand at the waterline. It's also quite here. Some people carried belongings over the water to turn lie on the quieter island. We didn't as we done want to get out backs wet.The little shop at the carpark sells souvenirs which are OK in price. Also toilets in the carpark for €0.50!I wouldn't make this trip again  but my kids are glad we went today.Also the bus journey is up across the mountains so if you don't like heights I would recommend this trip!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must, do it!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful clear water, first beach in Greece with white soft sand, similar to Cayo Coco, Cuba. Highly recommend it, nice drive thru the villages.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No pink sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful blue water but with the best will in the world can not discover pink sand.Way too busy. We turned right around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Arrive early to avoid disappointment
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What an absolutely lovely beach on the western side of Crete! With most popular destinations that tourists will flock to, getting here early to make the most of the beach and getting a good spot is paramount here. This review is based on our visit here in early July 2024. 1) It is quite a long and windy road to get here, if you are driving, you’d need to be a confident driver to navigate the narrow roads. 2) Parking - do not go to the first two places that will try and entice you in, go to the third parking place on the right where you pay €5 for the day upon leaving. 3) Sunbeds / Parasol. There’s plenty of choice if you get here early! We decided to opt for the parasols to the right and managed to get a sun lounger and the parasol at the front near the beach for €20 for a pair (it’s €5 extra if you want any more than two) 4) It will get busy so if you do arrive early, make the most of the water and empty space, busses and coaches full of people will eventually arrive - the beach is big enough to accommodate them all.5) The water is very clear and has some warm parts, it’s very child friendly as it goes up to knee hight, with the deepest park within the cove going up to roughly waist height. An absolutely beautiful beach with some elements of pink sand (not as pink as the heavily edited photos) and you can catch a wonderful sunset here. You can venture over to the other side, make sure you do, to discover another beach and pinkish sand! There is a bar which serves food and drink but will charge a lot more, I’d advise bringing your own food and drink and maybe use the bar/kiosk to buy an ice cream. There are toilets on site but they do charge €1 - we didn’t use them so I cannot say if they’re clean or not.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Be careful, on arrival you will necessarily be guided to Parking, the track is to go down and up on foot, it is not long and hard, about 10 min, but to plan in case of small children for example.At the beginning of the trail there is a supermarket that sells beach items, cremesolar etc...Paradise beach, to see early in the morning 9am max, before the massive arrival of buses, The water is crystal clear, this Pink sand is really original, there is foot far, the fish are numerous and not fierce to the rocks.The umbrella + deckchair is 20 €, then 5 € per additional deckchair.There is something to eat on site, a snack; where the staff is very friendly; offers sandwich, pizza, gyros, ice cream cold drinks... There are cabins to change and showers to rinse.The toilet is 1 € per person.ET!!! Once you get back to the car park, a person will stand in front of the car, asking you to pay 5 euros for parking.BUT it is a beach to see in his life! Happy holidays!! 🇬🇷

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just too many people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First the good - the water is stunningly blue and nice and shallow so you can go out pretty fat to paddle or swim and it feels very safe. There are lots of places to get drinks and food but thankfully they have not got greedy and things aren’t too expensive. Parking €5 a day, water €0.60 etc. Two sunbeds plus umbrella is €20 but get there early if you want one. I’m sure it’s a v beautiful place to be at 8am or 6pm…The bad - what makes this experience a 3 is the sheer volume of people there. You may as well be in Benidorm in the school holidays, barely a space on the sand and everyone packed in like sardines. Parking is pretty far away so a bit of a rocky trek to get to the beach, so watch out if you have mobility issues. It takes a long time to get there on very winding roads and do not get stuck behind coaches (they leave at 3pm). Is it worth it? Yes, but only out of season or very off peak times

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tip , Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach to visit there you will find: parking , umbrellas (if you arrive early) bar .Arrived do not stop at umbrellas but visit the beach across the shallow sea .A spectacle , if you need umbrella and towels you will find beautiful places .I recommend arriving early in the morning .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place ja nice beach. Sunbeds (20€ /pair) were little expensive. And it was a little bit hard to get down to the beach from the parking lot. But worth it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Mediterranean beach with a Caribbean feel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really beautiful beach, incredibly big with very clear and clean water. You can see the pink sand in many places, resulting from coral and shell deposits. Shallow and so suitable and safe for little kids. Only drawback is the long walk to reach the beach, dusty and uneven in places it might not be right for you if you have lots to carry or mobility issues. Take an umbrella with you or buy one (10eur) before you start the descent to the beach especially if you arrive late. You won't find a place to rent one down there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must if staying in western Crete
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is just as you see in photos! Stunning turquoise seas and some glimpses of pink sand. It is quite a walk from car parks- seems longer in the heat too. A sunshade of some sort is essential! Bar on beach very good prices. Parasols to hire bit pricey. Also a dry bag if you want to set up on island😉

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but too busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really pretty beach as long as you don't mind sharing a small amount of sand  with a huge amount of people. If you like lots of bodies on a beach then it's for you. If not drive along the coast road and find many other beaches not as crowded, but in my opinion far easier to access, and nowhere near as this tourist trap.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pink beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived here around 18 so we easily found free parking, otherwise cost parking 5 euro dia.Poi we walked to the beach it takes 10/15 minuti.Spiaggia rosa really , shallow water, beautiful evening waiting for the sunset

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, spotless, immense. Perfect for children. Nothing to say, perhaps the most beautiful beach I have ever visited.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Is more beautiful in Greece
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Camping insufficientToilets partially closedMinimarket not open at allRestaurant except pizza inedibleBe sure to take enough drinking water. Beach beautiful, butgives better

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice water but overflowing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clear water but soo crowded. Definitely be there early. We were there at 11:30 and all the beds were already occupied. If you keep to the right you come to a little quieter section and we bought an umbrella for 12€ upstairs before you run down. Is a good option though, this is nothing very firm in strong winds. And the blazing sun is too intense. Small snacks and drinks are available there. You also have to walk down and up again. Parking is available there for 5€. The path there is winding and the roads partly very narrow, but to create.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but lots of people.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We really wanted to see this beach and it would be beautiful without all the other people who also really wanted to see this beach!It was very overcrowded at 11.00 on a Friday in June.  There was very very little shade available. All the sun loungers and umbrellas were already taken so I purchased two from the shop adjacent to the car park but it was too windy to use them. The water was nice and warm and there were fish to be seen. We left after about an hour.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Big disappointment
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I wanted to discover this beach so much, unfortunately it was a great disappointment.It was like Palavas les Flots in the middle of August of the world to not finish... People were on top of each other.As for the pink sand I'm still looking for it...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bellissima!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach and lagoon are very beautiful, the water is crystal clear and transparent. The experience is definitely worth it, too bad it was really too crowded. I highly recommend bringing the umbrella, those available are few.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, worth a visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very nice beach to visit, beautiful color of water and sand.But the water is cold, there are not enough sunbeds and it is very crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: In short:
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, more than lagoon beach, very suitable for families with children shallow water and crystal clear sea... a little less for those who swim ad na. Unfortunately very little equipped and without showers with a dizzying ascent to made under the sun.... You can see very little pink. Beautiful and wild but too crowded wouldn't stay there again

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but not pink
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a beautiful beach. You must go early to enjoy it without there being too many people around. Also, do not go expecting to see a lot of pink sand as there is not a lot of it.  You will see more pink sand at Balos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beaches, historic places and etc
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An amazing place! With plenty of attractions for tourism with historical sites and a great reception, exotic food, just to remember I already miss

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Discovering paradise...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After a short walk feasible even with children, you arrive in this wonderful lagoon. Pink sand and clear water. Ideal place for children because flat and shallow water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise, but...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach, a true masterpiece of nature!! Only problem: MAN!!!! Before arriving at the beach a depressing work of cementation is underway 😣😣. Lots and lots of tourists (and we are only in June).... The entrance to the beach should be contingent to limit as much as possible the damage 🙏 otherwise in a few years there will be little and nothing of this paradise ...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must do experience!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is a must see experience! From the mountains on the way to the crystal clear waters when you're there. It is a very popular extraction so I would advise getting there early in the morning to ensure you get a sun lounger. We got there at 9:30am on a Sunday and had our pick on loungers. It got really busy from about 10:30-11am. When you walk onto the beach the main bit in front of you gets really busy so I'd advise going round the corner to the right where there are more loungers and we found it was a bit less crowded.The main car park is well sign posted and is at the bottom of the village. (Don't let the "parking attendants" flagging you down beforehand fool you as they are not part of the main car park, and you'll have further to walk down to the beach). The drive is quite the experience (in a good way!) Driving through and around the mountains.We brought our own food with us so I can't comment on the food prices but we did buy some alcoholic drinks from the huts on the beach which we thought were reasonably priced.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nothing special!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Touted as the best beach in Crete!!! Total disappointment if not for some nice onesBay off the beaten track. When we arrived it looked like a charnel house. Pink beach only on postcards! Islet crowded with tourists since early in the morning. Other bays and beaches are better, you can't understand the fame!!! Cheap beach or upon arrival stay to the right of the bay and continue on foot until you reach some small bays between the rocks that are worth the effort! The rest is completely commercial!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not worth it at all
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long, special drive there.Parking for a fee.Many, many hundreds of people flock there. Completely overcrowded.No shade to be found. No umbrellas or loungers available.No pink beach, no pink water, nothing, not nice.Not worth it at all

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach shame it will no be the same in a few years.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Possible was just wrong timing. Drove 2 1/2 hours from rethimno. Road winding and tight in places. Stunning views. Got to car parks like a concrete jungle. Acres of stone car parks full to bursting with cars and buses galore. Walk down on stone track. Through another area of gravel that was the previous car parking area possibly??  Like a flattened industrial estate.  Got to actual beach and sea 🌊 standing room only. There are lots of umbrellas with sun beds. Walked into sea with 100s of others and after 5 mins headed back to car for drive home. Stunning beach just over populated. Environmental disaster in the making.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mass tourism to the supposed hotspot - absolutely not recommended!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Buses full of day trippers make the pilgrimage to the supposed hotspot, only to find no sun loungers or no shaded place to lie down because everything is fenced in. The parking is OK at €5, but otherwise it's only worth visiting in the evening to enjoy the sea with definitely fewer visitors. It's quite exhausting for families with children, as there is a long, unshaded path down from the parking lot to the beach. The worst thing, however, is the crowds that are already there in June. I can't imagine what it's like there in August.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with plenty of people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach with hopelessly many people. We got there at 1130 paid 5euro parked.A good distance to walk from the parking lot down to the beach. There are always a lot of people down there, no sunbeds available, so bring your own chairs and parasol. Should have been there at 0900. We just turned around and went back to the hotel. Handicapped parking at the bottom of the gate, but not arranged to get a place all the way down.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tourist rip-off!⚠️⚠️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Attention!⚠️ Definitely not from June to October! It's a complete rip-off!!!😱😱😱it's like a herd migration, despite there being enough parking spaces you are redirected to private parking lots kilometers away! 😤😤😤

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach with great water.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Super beautiful beach with crystal clear water. You can walk hundreds of meters into the water.We arrived with a rental car without any problems. The road is completely asphalted up to the parking lot (5€). The way there over the mountains is super beautiful. A few narrower sections of the road, but no problem at all. I can't understand these negative comments at all.It's worth going there in the morning between 9 and 10 a.m., when it's still very empty. Later, from 11 a.m. to 12 p.m., the beach gets really busy. No problem in the water, but not so nice for photos.The infrastructure is there and the prices are really reasonable. It's not a Michelin-starred restaurant, but you can get decent sandwiches, etc.The walk from the parking lot takes about 10 minutes and you can even walk with a stroller.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but very crowded.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, turquoise waters good to swim in, clean...... but...... it was so crowded because it's so popular, this the only reason I couldn't give it a full 5,its a bit of a scetchy trek down from the car parks, so if your a bit infirm it may not be for you. We drove down from Chania on roads that are turbulent to say the least so to be honest wished we had picked another destination but Crete is a busy place now so it may not have been different anywhere else.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful pink beach, a UNESCO heritage site.Beautiful sea, lots of nature and still little invaded by humans.You can get there by leaving the vehicle about 700 meters from the beach, the road is quite comfortable even if there is gravel and dust.There is the possibility of renting umbrellas and sunbeds. Possibility to eat and drink something in the local kiosk, equipped with all services (free showers and paid toilets).The water is very shallow and crystal clear so there is the possibility of taking walks to reach the seabed that has emerged due to the effect of the tides.If you go to Crete you cannot visit Helafonissi.Stupendous

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and amazing water…
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had read reviews that this is a tourist trap which I try to avoid. Can't agree, the only thing that cost was €5 for the parking. Incredibly beautiful area with turquoise beautiful water. We swam a bit on the outskirts where the surfers hung out and it was clear, nice water... Food, coffee, drinks, toilets, showers are down by the sea. Everything you could need. The walk was neither long nor difficult despite 35* and bright sun. Nice to have visited this famous place 🌸💖

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but with many cons
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have known this beach for years and I think it's a shame how it has developed. The pros are:Nice, shallow, clear water, fine, clean sand, serviced, toilets available for €1.The cons: absolutely overcrowded, even in the off-season, far too few sun loungers/umbrellas, price for a set €20. No quiet spot in the water because the Instagram victims use the space for their pictures. The car park directly on the beach has been closed. Now you have to park about 3km away, for a fee of €5 and then walk 15 minutes to the beach (rough terrain).My conclusion: If you want to see the beach, you have to go extremely early (before 10:00 a.m.) It's worth a visit, but not if you want peace and quiet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but too many people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are no words to describe the beauty of this beach, but it is absolutely excessively crowded.To use the sunbeds and umbrella, you have to arrive at 8 in the morning, after two hours the beach is a mess.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Simply the most beautiful beach I have experienced! We arrived fairly early in the day and were able to obtain two beach chairs and umbrella. The food at the local food stand was fresh and delightful. The water and sand were soothing for my soul. Nothing negative here!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonisi Beach: never again!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The island of Crete has many beautiful beaches, one of the best is Falassarna beach. There is enough space there and the clean water is wonderfully turquoise to deep blue.But why some travel guides praise Elafonissi beach so much seems more than questionable.Depending on where your hotel is, you will arrive at this beach after a more or less long drive through the beautiful Topolia Gorge, and see huge parking lots filled with small rental cars for which you have to pay five euros.After that, you walk for about 20 minutes along the dusty road until you see the oh-so-popular beach. But the small beach is not only overcrowded with all the tourists who have come by themselves, but also with those who were in one of the many dozens of tour buses and who were carted here.If you love this kind of mass tourism, are happy with 1 m² of space on the beach and want to pay a lot for parking and beer: head to Elafonisi beach!Our conclusion: Elafonisi is at least as uninteresting and crowded as the Blue Lagoon in Malta.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointment
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very disappointed, first of all paid parking 5th, toilets 1st, a long walk and when you arrive it's crowded with people. We look for pink sand but I think that with the tourist surplus it is becoming more and more rare. Damage. The site, a few years ago, must have been splendid. Long road to be disappointed. It has become too touristy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hard to get to, pretty and busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Getting to this beach from Chania is a long 90 minute drive through narrow windy roads.   Most people seem to drive slow and cautiously, so it did not feel dangerous, although it did feel long. Once you finally get to the beach, there are several parking lots. The closest one to the end of the road charges five euro for the day. From there, it is a 5 to 10 minute walk down to the beach through a wide dirt road. It’s an easy walk. The beach is small for the number of people there and very very crowded. It is pretty, although not pink at all. They have a couple of snack bars and beach umbrellas for rent, if you are lucky enough to find an open one. There is also a water sports hut, offering windsurfing rentals, wingfoiling, and standup paddling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach if you come in March, but in June it is torture. It's so crowded that you can't even put up an umbrella.If you want to rent they charge you 20 euros, but that is free. Add 5 euros for the parking lot, from which you have a long stretch of relentless sun to get to.Add a hellish road from kissamos and you have a happy day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: אלפוניסי - אכזבה
reviewsWithKeywords.text: במילה אחת אכזבה! בכמה משפטים: יצאנו במיוחד מקאליבס ליום טיול לחוף אלפוניסי וכמה אתרי תיור מעניינים בדרך (אגיה סופיה למשל מומלץ), כשהגענו לאזור החוף הסתבר שהחניות רחוקות מאוד! (לרדת לחוף מילא אבל כל הדרך חזרה בעליה ובחום לא שווה את המאמץ. אגב חניה, תתעלמו מהמכוונים בסרבלים צהובים ותמשיכו להתקדם עם הרכב הכי קרוב לחוף שניתן (הראשונים פשוט חאפרים ויכוונו אתרם לחניות רחוקות מדי). חוץ מזה, חיפשנו חול/מים ורודים - לא מצאנו! חיפשנו שירותים או מלתחות נאותות - לא מצאנו ברמה נאותה! חיפשנו סככות או כסאות ים - לא מצאנו בכמות מספקת! חיפשנו ברזיות או מקלחות מים מתוקים - כמעט ואין! בקיצור, רוצים ים צלול וחופים נהדרים חפשו באזור אלמרידיס, קאליבס, רתימנו ועוד. חוץ מזה אהבנו את כרתים והיא אהבה אותנו בחזרה.In a word disappointment!  In a few sentences: we especially left Kalyves for a day trip to Elafonissi beach and some interesting sightseeing sites on the way (Agia Sophia for example recommended), when we arrived at the beach area it turned out that the parking spaces are very far away! (Going down to the beach filled but all the way back uphill and in the heat not worth the effort.  By the way, ignore those aiming in yellow jumpsuits and continue to proceed with the vehicle closest to the beach possible (the former are simply diggers and will direct their site to parking spaces that are too far away).  Besides, we were looking for pink sand/water - we couldn't find any! We were looking for proper amenities or wardrobes - we couldn't find an adequate standard! We were looking for sheds or sea chairs - we couldn't find enough of it! We were looking for faucets or freshwater showers - almost none! In short, want clear sea and great beaches Look in the area of Almeridis, Kalyves, Rethymno and more.  Other than that we loved Crete and she loved us back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonissi - never again!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Warning about Elafonissi: We were there at the beginning of June. Even at this early time of the season, the lagoon is hopelessly overcrowded. By mid-morning, all the sun lounger sets were sold out. Most of the visitors who came in during the day couldn't even find a shady spot on the edge. We were lucky to find a small shady spot for our towels in a corner. That didn't stop a group of six people from crawling over to us, so that one lady almost lay on our towel. We have been to Crete several times and will definitely come back. But we have definitely crossed Elafonissi off our list. If you travel by rental car, you will find many beautiful beaches with few visitors, especially on the south coast.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip with own car
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow is all i can say this beach is sooo beautiful we arrived 1700 in the evening when the daytime tourists had been and gone it exceeded my expectations however word of warning to those who dont like heights the drive to get to it are hairpin roads sheer drops but oh so very beautiful the views enroute even if heights scare you are amazing and worth it  we stayed for about 90 mins just walking paddling taking in the sight not commercialised at all but   through the various villages enroute were tavernas restaurants and souvenir shops  dotted around. Would highly recommend hiring car and going to this beautiful beach our car was 50 euros and 20 euros petrol for the day but we saw loads of tourist attractions and some not tourist places that would never have got to see on a tour and saved money as the trip through company would have been 30 euros each

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach in Crete!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Blue-green transparent waters, shallow, suitable for children. Westerly wind (the one that catches all over western Greece) from noon onwards, so prefer a morning bath!! And don't listen to the naysayers about the walk, it's a 10 minute uphill road at least.. with a wonderful view for photos

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, no shade
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The lagoon is wonderful and the water is clear and warm. It really does have a Caribbean feel to it. Unfortunately, there are far too few umbrellas and loungers or the possibility of finding a shady spot. You have to be very sun-resistant to lie in the blazing sun for 4 hours and wait for the bus to come back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: FANTASTIC!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is one of the few beaches in Crete that is famous for its blue-green waters, combined with the incredible natural landscape. Prefer the small beaches located on the islet after the lagoon, as long as you have the patience to walk there. The tranquility and beauty of the landscape will compensate you to the fullest. In several places and especially in the parts of the island, you can see the pink sand from the corals. It is worth visiting at least once. P.S.: The parking of the car is done at a long distance from the beach necessarily, either at any point, or in a parking lot by paying 5 euros. It's a good idea to equip yourself with water bottles and an umbrella.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches we have visited. The drive was a little scary some high mountains and no barriers. Scenery is lovely though. Car park €5 for the day which isn’t too bad. Walk down to beach you needed to be careful on the rocks. Toilets were €1Beach was busy but to be expected.Water was clear and traces off pink sand were visible. Water was lovely and you could go out as far as you wanted.Well worth the drive to see and to spend a good few hours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, white sand and low waters ideal for families with young children. It is a 5 minute walk from the car park and can be very busy even in the off season.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Vastly Overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Vastly overrated. Pleasant enough but nothing spectacular, and although traces of pink could be seen if you looked hard enough it’s a real stretch to call the sand pink. People were packed like sardines even in relatively slow times. Nice scenery on both of the main roads leading to the beach. In all honesty not worth the considerable effort to get there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: OVERRATED
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Only positive point: the crystal clear water 🌊The negative points : - a commercial beach, everything is paid for (parking, deckchair, parasols, etc.)- a beach crowded with people- be wary of retouched images... you have to look and be very vigilant to see the few grains of pink sandNot worth the detour…

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You can but you don't have to
reviewsWithKeywords.text: OVERRATED OVERRATED AND OVERRATED AGAIN. It's miles away from pink. Mass tourism like no other. You'll have to pay €5 for parking BUT: what's on offer is ridiculous. If you want to lie down (lounger with umbrella €25) or stand on the beach (which is anything but pink) with what feels like 100,000 people, then you've come to the right place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Yes for the beach, no for the pink sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very pretty beach, but you have to go early, it fills up quickly and we were there in May. in high season it must be crowded. if you go there for the “pink sand” on the other hand, forget it!!   it is barely visible. disappointment. If you are looking for a place to eat, go without hesitation to the Taverna Kalomirakis Family, very warm welcome and very good meal at reasonable prices.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: good but nothing more
reviewsWithKeywords.text: pretty but less than what people say the sand is more slightly pink in places. more touristy and oversold than it's worth the sand is wet so laying out your towel is complicated. there is no toilet shade available for a fee 1st

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise & more
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lot of points to share 1. Public Transport to elafonisi  - absolutely convenient , from KTEL central bus station Chania - reach by 8.30 and the bus is at 9 , buy tickets from window , 22 euro return journey (43.90 precisely for couple) . They take out your bags and keep in storage area of bus , except water & your cross bag nothing is allowed so finish your coffee & croissants before entering. There is a good outlet at bus station to enjoy a coffee and snack if you have started early & had no time for breakfast. 8.45 boarding starts & 9 sharp bus leaves. It took us 2 hrs ( goes via Kismoss) , buses comfortable, AC . Scenic journey through mountains ( left side) , sea views( right) . Bus waits whole day at the beach parking & return at 16.00 hrs ( in Chania around 17.30 return was faster than going) . From parking you will walk a kilometer or so to reach the actual beach . 2. What to carry - food: at the parking itself there is a nice shop that sells food & drinks , other accessories. It is decently priced with chicken beef sandwiches etc at 3.50 euro and water big bottle 1. Euro, ice creams 2.50 ish and other bakery products like pies , vegan option available too. So as you get down you can pick your picnic but only hitch is half of the bus crowds enters the shop & it’s queued . I carried our own picnic , mat . Beach umbrellas seats are sold at 20 euro 5 euro extra bed. It’s super sunny and there is absolutely no shade where you can lay your mat. So if possible carry a beach umbrella or be prepared to stay under sun or spend 20 euros. At the beach itself there was just 1 shop half closed half open ( may 20,2024) may be in summer there will be more but best is to have your food drinks stock with you . 3. The beach - the beach is dreamy & a must visit I will say. The waters is like Maldives , crystal clear blue with soft white sand. Best for kids & non swimmers . It’s in fact a very different beach than I have ever seen sure you can have spots with deep water to swim but the main attraction is the 2 lagoon like beach sections yes sections as first 1 kilometer of stretch is shallow ( and such wide stretch ) and you can literally walk through to reach the another small sand bay which again is extended to next water stretch again walkable , standable. How much crowded it gets you can still find your private spot to swim it’s that large & wide. Water shines like diamonds & truly it’s magical . Kids & adult both will be smitten by its beauty. There are restrooms 1 euro , covered changing spots free. 4. Pink sand - yes the sand appears as white at first but as you enter more and especially at second lagoon you see stretches of pink colour , it’s beautiful truly . You can easily carry your mobile or camera and take pics , let your hat & sun glasses stay on you as the beach is more like a huge huge salt water swimming pool without waves , calm absolutely. You have to experience its beauty to know what I am saying . 5. Return: my advice is carry your picnic and save budget for return snacks. After swim & change to be in bus if 4 you must leave the beach atleast at 15.15 to walk comfortably and reach parking by 15.45 . It’s a mild uphill & sun is sapping your energy. Then you can enjoy an ice cream in the parking shop . So much worth the expense 😀. Bus leaves sharp at 4.00 and I think KTEL is doing a fabulous job for people without car. 6. For those who drive , ample parking available at euro 5 ( I assume for day ) and roads are good , steep mountain curve so be prepared for showing off your good driving skills . If you have car I will suggest come by 15.00 do sun is milder and beach gets emptier with all bus crowd returning . Sun sets are beautiful & dreamy I have heard not seen. Hope this helps , enjoy your visit . You will see lot of olive trees. I did not take much pictures as I loved to swim more but there are plenty of pictures on google & I confirm that matches the site.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. Crystal clear water and pinkish tinged sands at the shore. You can walk out a long distance, including to and around the island.  Be prepared for a little walk from the parking areas. Bathrooms (1 Euro) and some food is available at the beach. Drive from Chania is pretty, but the small mountain roads can be congested. Great mountain, gorge, and small village views along the way. We took a different route along the coast back to Chania to avoid traffic. It was beautiful but full of harrowing switchbacks, so I suggest sticking with the main roads (Google map directions).  A set of lounge chairs and tiki umbrella was 20 Euro, but they fill up fast.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: a site to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pretty beach, reception from the well-organized parking lot. The space and the beach are magnificent.Staff on site welcoming and at your disposal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too expencive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Beach itself is nice, but the sunbeds are 20 € a pair in May! That is just a bit too expencive. Also the parking is 1 km away from the beach and it cost 5€. The road down to the beach is not that easy to walk, so good shoes is a benefit. I do not recommend, it's not worth the money.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sandy beach that shimmers slightly pink. Very gently sloping beach, so very suitable for children. We were there on Sunday and it was very busy.The parking fee of 5 euros is fair, as there are actually no additional costs. The toilets are awful, hygiene is a foreign word here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nice beach but sand not necessarily pink
reviewsWithKeywords.text: In May there were relatively few people but in high season it must be crowded. Still worth seeing. It's easy to access and there are still a few places with shade. The water was too cold for us but people were swimming (shallow water)We were supposed to see the beach during a plane flight but the wind did not allow us to go that far.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lafonisi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Charge 5 euros for parking. The mini market is expensive. Charge to use the toilet. Twenty euros for the sunbeds, and the employees are rude, too bad I thought they were old men in Crete, and how the lavender characterizes them, but it was lost as it seems and false magic took its place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't waste your day,  overrated.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Elafonisi "Pink beach " You'll read online that this is one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe. This is in our view an overstatement.
