Elafonisi is nice but nothing that takes your breath away. In all honesty it is EXTREMELY OVER-RATED and looks nothing like the tour brochures you'll see or what they want you to believe. The drive will literally drive you to drink 🤣 or want to. Winding narrow roads,  sometimes with sheer drops at the side of them.  No wonder they have a RAKI house on the way 🤣 Difficult at times for 2 cars to pass,  so imagine a bus 😳 as you'll see in one of the photos. You have to be extremely careful, especially after stopping by the RAKI house 🤣which is highly recommended before and after. There's a tunnel that is barely as wide as the car,  its one way and not very well lit, even with your lights on, it's along the winding road with next to nothing for a barrier. There's a light along the drive that tells you when you can drive through the tunnel.  I couldn't enjoy the drive back up...it was so stressful when the bus turned the corner and the vehicles coming down had to back up in order for him not to drive off the road.  Extremly narrow in some parts including through the villages, so imagine the heart of tourism.  No thanks!!!The mountains are stunning driving down but hard to enjoy with your focus on the narrow passages.  Like my companion said you have to focus on the road otherwise you'll go over the cliff.  I think if you insist on seeing Elafonisi that a boat tour is better. There were very small traces of pink in the sand where the sea laps the shore and that was about it. Nothing spectacular. Lots of parking for 5€ , but the walk down the gravelly road is not wheelchair accessible and you have to watch your step regardless so you don't twist your ankle.  The walk down to the beach and back up is an arduous one especially in the boiling sunshine. Signage isn't that great for trails that take you down to the beach.Walking back.... humid as hell.  Make sure you have lots of water on hand. 10+  minutes from the parking lot to the beach. To use the toilet,  if that's what you want to call them it will cost you 1€And to rent a beach chair is 20€ for 2/10€ each. 2.5x more than other parts of the island that rent lounge chairs, which have much more to offer in facilities, accommodation and scenery.  Beach chairs packed like sardines with tourists.  Windy as hell, apparently even in the heart of summer its known to be quite windy. Only a couple of cafes and slim pickings for accommodation. Massively over populated beach with tourists before the heart of the season.  Very shallow water that's great for kids.Would I go back? NoWhy? Because there are many other places on Crete that have beautiful sandy beaches, turquoise glistening sea and views that will take your breath away.  The drive from Kaliviani Kissamou to Elafonisi took an hour. It will be a nightmare in the heart of tourism. We returned to our glorious accommodation after less than 2 hours at Elafonisi and reserved for an additional night before leaving the area.Our accommodation was the highlight of our adventure as well as the scenic boat tour to Gramvousa and Balos Lagoon which are worth the time to visit. This is my honest review based on my personal experience and I know my companion agrees with me 100%.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not so pink as you think
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Convenient parking right next to the attraction, 5 euros for the whole day. The beach is not as pink as in the colored photos, but it is still impressive. Hot water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good, not great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We read that this was one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe and drove 2.5 hours to explore. It really is a beautiful beach but very crowded. We arrived at noon so maybe it would be better if you got there really early. We parked and walked abt 20 mins to get to the beach, which I don’t really mind. It was an easy walk.  The pink sand was just sorta pink. All in all, I’m not sure I would go again just because of the crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not as in pictures
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach, but not with pink colors in the sand while we were there. First of the season with good space, and clean and tidy.Stand cafe with ok prices and good service

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's really worth the getaway. Beautiful wherever you look at it. We went from Gouves Beach, about 7 hours round trip is worth it. 5 euros for parking and a bit of walking. The landscape is crazy!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach! 🌊😍
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is stunning with beautiful clear waters and a pleasant temperature, making it a fantastic place to relax and enjoy. Keep in mind that there isn't much shade, so come prepared. You'll park your car and walk a few minutes to reach the beach, but it's worth the effort. There's also a canteen on the beach in case you get hungry. All in all, this is a must-visit beach! 🏖

reviewsWithKeywords.title: PARADISE
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach that looks like it's from another planet, the water is clear with shades of turquoise. The sand, imagine it's pink, only access is a little difficult, but it's worth it as I took wonderful photos of the mountains.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We used a tour operator who took us back to this magnificent beach with translucent water. Wonderful !! The water is not pink as shown in the photos but it remains a very beautiful beach. When you arrive at the car park, it takes 10 minutes to walk to the beach. Toilets cost 50 cents near the parking lot and 1 euros on the beach. there is a bar at the entrance which is shaded which is not the case on the beach. Bring a hat, good cream and water because it can be very hot there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning Beach. Despite cold water in early May, we loved the beach nonetheless. It’s a gorgeous beach. Anyone who says otherwise isn’t being accurate.I’d read reviews mentioning challenges parking, a long walk to the beach and crowds. In early May, we had no trouble parking our car or finding a private spot further down the beach. The walk from parking isn’t short, but it’s absolutely worth it unless you’re hauling a lot of stuff or not able to walk very well. No beach is fun when overcrowded so I can’t speak as to peak season, but I can confirm that the beach is beautiful and with warm water it must be amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unfortunately, to flee
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place, really, but too touristy. I can't imagine in the middle of summer...Non-existent pink sand. Too much road for nothing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Suffering
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you exclude the beautiful beach, you will leave there with a cold from the wind that blows all day, and it will make your nerves ragged, the weather is not even a correct forecast because the place is completely western and you will find yourself in front of surprises with the weather. Never again, unless you are nearby and want to go for a bit and a dare... Taverns are also very expensive...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely worth doing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach... leaves you speechless..Despite the wind we still managed to swim... the water was cold but bearable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach  a must see !!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach with pink sand.  Amazing shallow water which links to other parts of the island. Well worth visiting especially  if you're staying in Western Crete. There's plenty of space to  get away from the crowds which is what I  prefer to do.  If you want to avoid the crowds then best to go early in the morning before the boats of tourists arrive or  and even better option would be to rent one of the  nice apartments on top of the hill so that way you can have the place to yourself and take in the incredible sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: As everyone says, busy and beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 5 stars for nature doing its thing and being amazing. 0 stars for the over-tourism here. And yes I know we are all to blame! Elafonisi beach really is stunning, I’ve never seen such clear and shallow waters that reach for metres and metres out to sea. Plus the fish life is also incredible and they get so close! I spent ages just watching them dart around below, so clear and right there. We knew it would be a bit of a risk going at the very start of the tourist season but we so wanted to see it for ourselves and we stayed only an hour away.We walked the track from the car park which was pleasantly empty when we arrived at around 11am on an early May Thursday, and turned left as we got to the beach, finding a small little mini-beach between the rocks with only one other couple. Maybe we had something good going on here, we thought, as we watched the main beach get busier and busier and busier. But alas, after an hour or so of blissful solitude, exploring the waters on our little patch, more humans kept flooding in to our little cove and just did not stop to the point where we were squashed up against the rocks of our little sandy patch, by the sea. We called it a day after sticking it out for about 3 hours and so wanting to make the most of the most incredible sea waters we’ve ever seen, and headed back to the calm of our AirBnB for the afternoon. I think it would be a real gem to see the natural beauty of this place in the middle of a cold December or January for example. I don’t even know what the solution is with places like this! It will only get worse through the season and through the years and this was only May. We came, we saw, we left, we’ve ‘done’ it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ugh
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A lot of overrated opinions for this beach in my opinion.The pink sand is minimal and the place is crowded with people so it is difficult to enjoy it during the summer.so-so

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pink sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very relaxing place with a pink sand beachOn the other hand, I recommend taking a hotel because the road is tiring if you come from the Heraklion side.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Totally disappointed with this beach, the pink sand, almost non-existent, you have to know it and look carefully to see it. Even if the landscape is magnificent, this beach is not worth the detour.We preferred the Balos lagoon 100 times despite the gray weather and the difficult access road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Parking scam
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We are returning from Elafonisi Square.Magnificent place with a dream landscape. T⁰ideal and uncrowded in the season.A pleasant time with the family until we left by car where we were asked to pay 5 euros for 2 hours of unspecified parking at the entrance.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but worth it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Superb site which is worth it after a 3.5 hour drive from Heraklion, including 37 km in 1 hour in the mountains.The pink sand can be seen but is not obvious.At this time not too many people but in summer it must be hell.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Magnificent beach. Visit the island on foot. Large sand dunes. Small coves. Very pleasant for swimming despite the wind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit April 2024
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Magical place.Heavenly beach with the mountain in the background. A true taste of paradise. It’s really something to see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach with lots of nooks and crannies and easy access
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Splendid place! The water is turquoise, the sand pink. Access is easy, parking (paid) right next door and several restaurants (only one open at the beginning of April). You only have to walk 10’ to get to the beach. We also went to Balos but we preferred this beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: İt's an amazing beach with the pink sands although a difficult transport there. Maybe reaching it with a boat tour is better.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with clean water. Beautiful surroundings and a nice place to relax, enjoy the weather and swim. However, we were just a little disappointed that the sand is nowhere near as pink as it is described and seen in pictures online.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blue-green magic!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with turquoise waters! Another magical beach of Crete! You should definitely visit it! Magic!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very pretty, LOTS of people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had high expectations regarding this pink sand beach, often listed as the best in the world. You have to spend a lot of time getting there, from Heraklion it is more than 3 hours, from Chania an hour and a half.Upon arrival it is very poorly organized, the parking lot is very far away, you have to walk quite a bit with a strong sun between stones and dirt. Now on the beach the sand is not as pink as in the photos, only in small stretches and there are a lot of people and wind. There are no services, bathrooms with queues and very few, the spaces to disturb on the beach are taken by stalls where they charge, generally very messy and expensive.We walked towards the central point and things improved a lot there. Fewer people, more depth and turquoise colors in the water and a bit of the famous pink sand. Bellaplaya but complicated, I would not return.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must-do on Crete!  We enjoyed the drive and had a great time at the beach, but please load up on SPF!  We saw so many people burnt to a crisp and even got burnt ourselves despite using sunscreen.  The sun is no joke here.  The pink sand isn't as pink everywhere as social media portrays it to be -- but it's there!  The water was clear and beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Give it a miss unless out of season.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is so sad.  We went to Elafonisi many times - but over 10 years ago.  What on earth have they done to it!.  The beach and water cannot have changed but we couldn’t see it for hordes and hordes of sun beds (hugely expensive) and even more hordes of people.  Parking was a Joke - an absolute free for all.  If lucky enough to find a space you then cannot find any shade at all or in fact any space to sit sun or shade!Admittedly we were there in August last year so expect crowds but not on that scale.I think the only time to see it as it should be seen is to go very out of season.  If you can’t do that then really don’t bother - there are many other lovely places on Crete.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Morning/Day Trip to Elafonissi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved going to this beach! It was a very cloudy day which made it actually too cold to swim in the late spring time, but we greatly enjoyed the trip nonetheless. We drove about 1.5 hours from Kissamos down a very scenic drive (just don’t do it if it’s going to rain/storm!) through the mountains. There we stops for food along the way, which we used on the way back for a lovely cafe lunch. The beach itself had plenty of parking if you arrive EARLY (8am-9am). Once we left around noon, a flood of people arrived (off of cruise ships docked nearby it seemed), along with a storm. The beach is huge, unique, diverse, and truly beautiful even from the ground view. Bathrooms require payment, be prepped, and they made us pay for seats even though we left soon after arriving due to the rain storm, which wasn’t very fair. But the location itself was wonderful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The blue paradise of Chania
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Elafonisi is more than just an island; it's a paradise.The beach boasts a remarkable diversity: tranquil coves for those seeking an easy swim, rocky areas perfect for snorkeling (with an impressive array of fish), deeper waters catering to experienced swimmers, a shallow bay ideal for children; there is a place where water sports enthusiasts can rent boats, but we didn't reach it.There are both organized beaches, requiring tourists to pay a fee, and free beaches, especially in the dunes area.Access to Elafonisi is possible both by water and public transport. From the north coast of the island, you can reach it from Chania or, even more conveniently, from Kissamos. However, it's advisable to book your ticket in advance, as the two or three daily runs are insufficient to accommodate the large number of tourists eager to visit the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful without tourists
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was amazing! it was very nice weather and the beach was empty and beautiful. The sunset was magical. no coaches and endless tourists are fantastic!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beaches are magnificent. The water is cool and the coasts windy, we went there at the beginning of June, it must be different in summer. The landscape is wonderful. The children have fun and can have fun peacefully.As for parking, don't stop at the 1st one when you arrive, there are several further down as you get closer to the beaches. It is truly a place to see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lagoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a shame that the water was cold (September). There are also very dirty corners, humans don't respect anything. Too much people...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Handsome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The place is beautiful, the water fantastic. Clearly you have to take into account that there are many tourists and that a strong wind often blows.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: THE beach to go to near Chania
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful beach, chairs available for rent, very good restaurant on the beach, easy access and they deliver to your beach chair

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Boccaperta😜
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After twenty years it has evolved touristically but still quite natural, no longer wild as it once was but always enchanting especially in this season.Breathtaking 😎

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I have seen in my life. Not very difficult to reach, it is always very crowded, but thanks to its vastness it holds up well to the impact... Just don't stop at the first umbrellas... A bit of a walk is worth the view. The services are well maintained (free bathrooms and showers) but they are close to the car parks, so to enter the wildest and most beautiful part you need to go with a minimum of organization (umbrellas, water etc.) unless you want to go back to "the civilization". There are some designated areas where you cannot enter to protect the landscape and that seems correct to me. Highly recommended place for snorkeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A postcard place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A wonderful place which, even if it has undergone strong tourist exploitation in the last decade, remains a naturalistically intact place. A beach like no other in Europe, a lagoon with shallow water where you can walk in the water for hundreds of metres. Crystal clear water, shades of blue, emerald green and turquoise, pink and golden sand frame this wonder. There are two or three bars on the beach where you can buy food and drinks at average prices. It's an easy walk to get to the beach from the car park. In high season there are a lot of people but in June the beach was very liveable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning paradise...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking Beach.  Crystal blue and turquoise water as far as your eyes can see. Soft sand, some pink sand at the waters edge. I must see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous slice of paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really amazing beaches, all with slightly different characters and all idyllic.We went in October at the end of the season and it was busy, I imagine in peak season it would be too crowded to enjoy fully- October definitely a good time to go. Really stunning place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Only for instagram photos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Positive: Excellent beach suitable for familiesDisabled access to the shoreNegative: from the parking lot you have to walk on an uneven dirt road for 15 minutes (with the watch!!!!) ....1€ toilet fee. (Don't get lucky!!!!) …..5€ parking fee….20€ the set of sunbeds …..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Finally car...out!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Elafonissi is certainly one of the most beautiful places on the Cretan coast. And finally the authorities realized that a first step to guarantee its best conservation was to remove cars, coaches and campers by setting up parking lots a few hundred meters away. Furthermore, the access areas on the dunes have been demarcated. Well done. Although it is difficult to keep thousands of people at bay every day. Even in October at the end of the season.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the drive to get there! Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach - remote and beautiful, really worth the slightly tough drive to get there! The water is just fabulous, if you like a little adventure and nice beach -- this is a must do!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good place not to miss once in Crete
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is large and ideal for families with young children. Laggon is very shallow water, water is very clear. You can spend 2-8h all day if you like.Just remember to drive down the whole street and do not get fooled from "official parking place guides" - there are 2 or 3 parking lots private but directly before beach is the Mega Parking for beach and costs as well 5€, but you save 1km walking......

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach...a beautiful experience starting from the journey to reach this magnificent beach...a Caribbean sea...comfortable services on the beach...possibility of having lunch on the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely beach, definitely overhyped though!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a long old drive across to Elafonsi from Chania but with some lovely little villages and sights on the way as you make your way through winding narrow roads, sometimes with sheer drops at the side of them. Anyway about the beach. It's one of the nicest beaches we've ever visited, however it's seriously overhyped and looks nothing like the pictures you'll see in tour guide brochures. There are very small traces of pink in the sand where the sea laps the shore but that's about it.  We visited in late October on a weekday. It was quite busy but not to the point it was uncomfortable. The water was crystal clear, warm and shallow, making it a safe place for families or those that are not strong swimmers.When you arrive, ignore the people trying to persuade you to park on their premises and keep driving until you can't drive any further. You'll get to some bollards in the road and just before them on the right hand side is the closest car park, with plenty of spaces. It costs 5 Euros to park for the day. The walk down to and back up from the beach is a bit of an arduous one, especially in the boiling sunshine.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Area, Heaving With People
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a lovely area with fantastic extended beach. The throngs of people, even late in the season, makes it less than relaxing, however. Go as far out as you can,and enjoy the shallow waters

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches you’ll ever see !!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and is as shown, sand is white and where the shore meets the sand, that is where there are pink patches. Water is clean and clear with very good visibility and you can see your feet until you can’t stand. The beach has plenty of Nissis where the sand and see meet to form water that looks like ice. Gorgeous and would recommend to anyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Doesn't necessarily have to be...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very crowded. The beach is beautiful, the water is clear and nice and shallow, but not as special as advertised. The pink strip with shell limestone is very narrow and you have to look for it. There are certainly equally beautiful bays on Crete that you can enjoy in peace...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: King & Queen + prince
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beach paradise, fantastic water, a interesting bus trip with narrow roads and mountains to go there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy commercial beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you like crowds this is for you . We went mid - October, mid week, dread to think what main holiday season would be like car park is 5euro,  if you want the toilet it’s 1 euro, dread to think where people who don’t want to pay go 🙀- just not our cuppa

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A paradise on earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach I have ever been to is not only beautiful, with beautiful shades of the sea in every possible blue color, but also wonderful exotic vegetation and wonderful sand on the beach. We were lucky because in October there were no crowds on this beach and we could enjoy the charm of the island and the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely worth it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful drive there, some parts in the rain can accommodate 1 car and the tunnel was also an experience. Parking for the whole day is 5 euros, you have to walk a bit to get there, but then you have something. Come on. early because it will be busy later in the day. Find a spot on the other side, where it is much quieter. Nice area for snorkeling. There is not much pink sand, but it can be found. Keep it clean, it is a unique area but definitely worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: How to spoil one of your best natural assets
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just come back from a wasted trip to Elafonisos beach. (The spelling is taken from my Cretan map.)  I should have been pre warned by the packed car parks; must have been well in excess of 1000 cars plus coaches and this in October.  Heaven only knows what high season is like.The trek down to the beach is past tavernas and souvenir sellers and once you get there, rows of sunshades and beds and people, so many  people.On a positive note, the water IS crystal clear in amazing shades of blue and turquoise and I've no doubt that without all the humanity, it is quite spectacular. Unfortunately tourism has not done it any favours.  Such a shame.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise, indeed!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The finest beach in the world is this one. It took me 4 hours to get there from the other side of the island, and I wish I could have stayed longer since it truly is a captivating paradise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's high time that people question themselves!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I will give 3 stars out of 5. Not for the site it is but for the sadness of tourism.I went scuba diving there, I was able to admire the clarity of the water and the beauty of the fine white sand. Gorgeous ! I was also able to admire paper towels, cigarette butts and trash in what nature offers us. A gold star also to those who collect pink sand to take home as a souvenir. In a few years, thanks to you, there will be no more. People's selfishness will never stop...Apart from that, bring a small vest anyway because it is very windy. Also bring a small snack because there really isn't much "food" there. Paying toilets (1€), I do not condone. People go into the bushes to do what creates papers all over the beach.In summary, a beautiful place which will gradually be destroyed by mass tourism.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pink Sand. Very busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful, the most striking thing is the pink sand. Otherwise it is very crowded and overexploited. The parking lots are a little far away for traveling with small children, although access is easy. It is worth visiting although there are better beaches in Crete

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too many people and that’s in October!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with clear water and pink sands HOWEVER far too many prople bus loads and car parks full Note it’s 5 euros a day to park and 2 sunbeds and an umbrella is 20 euros! 1 euro to use the WC! Signs show it’s a place of natural wonders however too many people lots of rubbish and deserted caravans upon entry Such a shame

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crete's most beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with sandy bottom and blue sea. Definitely worth a visit. Parking for 5 euros for the whole day. From the square there is a long way down to the water, be careful about what you take to the beach. Definitely worth a visit. However, we remember that 10-15 years ago you could park closer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonissi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful place, worth visiting. Beautiful nature, rich life in the water. Lovely place. the day we were there it was very windy. We experienced a sandstorm 😅 😂 it is recommended to check the weather beforehand - we have done it anyway but did not expect it to be as troublesome as it actually was. TO faith in all things beautiful 🙂Parking 5 euros

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even a large crowd of tourists will not be able to spoil the impressions of the beach. Don't expect pink sand all over the beach. Pink stripes can be seen on the surf line (0.5-1m), and this is also very beautiful. Expensive to the beach - this is a real paradise, I think everyone should see it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonissi - only pink in June and 14 days into July
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our son and daughter-in-law visited Elafonissi Beach a few years ago - the most beautiful thing they had seen. So we rented a car here in September. - drove across Crete and reached Elafonissi which was absolutely packed with SO many people. Impossible to find a place to be. There was at this time of year - NO pink beach. If you want to see it, it must come in June and 14 days into July - the pink mussels search deeper in the high season and return in March. Access to the beach is definitely not for the faint of heart - due to large stones and very, very uneven.This review so you don't spend a whole day there in vain. The Greeks visit the beautiful place every year in June and early July...we would have greatly appreciated if we had been informed about all this.We had - on top of that - spoken to a guide the day before about the trip and were told that it was very beautiful, but nothing about the conditions at this time of year.There are SO many other beautiful beaches with the cleanest water.This review, so you don't run after an experience that can only be seen in June / July

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mixed feelings about this
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Do you like hard winds with sand smattered all over your body into you pores? Then this is the place to go! Road there is managable but not so pleasant, of course, you couldnt expect more.( We drove from Galatas)Looks like roads children paint in kindergarten. The beach is very beautiful though. May be worth a visit. Im glad im home.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Former paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bitter disappointment. Hordes of tourists, paid parking (5€), paid bathroom (1€) and valets who have to sort the constant coming and going of cars and buses. After parking, there is a walk under the scorching sun to arrive at a beach covered with rude swimmers. The pink sand can barely be seen. The shallow water makes you think more of a swamp than a paradise beach. We took a drive and ran away.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointment
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ultra crowded beach. From this year you will pay 5 euros for parking. The rental of umbrellas and sunbeds has shameful prices. 10 years ago 7 euros umbrella + 2 sunbeds and the rest free, obviously. The party's over, drop the buck

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beach that can be reached with difficulty by car via two routes, the internal mountainous one 44 km and the coastal one 54 km, both very dangerous, the guard rails were almost completely missing, narrow roads which had more right of passage for donkeys, sheep and goats👀🤦🏻‍♀️😂, the Greek guide leaves much to be desired but….Elafonissi is beautiful, so it was worth the trip! There are bars, taverns, hotels, small shops, public toilets, umbrella with 2 sunbeds for €15, but if you go in the morning you can fully enjoy everything, after 11am various buses arrive and lots of people in cars (parking for €5 before going down to the beach) and there are waves of people chasing the umbrella 🤦🏻‍♀️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful place with translucent waters. It is advisable to get there early if you want to enjoy the place before the tourist buses arrive... and choose a parasol on the beach.However, be careful with the images seen on the internet, the sand is not pink everywhere, which does not detract from the beauty of the place however.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely go😎🏝️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were there early at 9.30 a.m. on the recommendation of our hosts... and had an "almost" free choice of loungers and umbrellas 😎Parking space 5 euros is okayGetting 3 loungers and 1 umbrella for 25 euros is also okayGreat clean beach. Snack stand at normal prices.Beach wasn't as crowded as we feared... just get there early. We were there for about 5 hours.Great water... wonderful 🏝️🌞

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonisi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach, evocative scenery, breathtaking viewThe only flaw for those like me who struggle with anxieties is the journey to reach this wonderful paradise! The journey is a bit long and the curves, the height and the absence of gardareil in some parts are not the best! However, it is worth making this effortI recommend going very early to find space in the areas or bring at least an umbrella with you

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic place!!! TO
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful water, and very fine sand, ideal place for those with children, if you want to use the Lo Scosiglio lido (umbrellas attached) umbrella cost €20 1 deckchair €5, on the coast there are kiosks for eating and drinking, accessible for disabled people. If you want to stay calm in uncontaminated nature you can walk a little and find solitary places, as it is very crowded (But it's worth it!!!)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Prepare yourself for the sad spectacle!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: And yes, we knew it but what a shame!!!4th time in Crete in the last 10 years, we wanted to finally see this beautiful and famous beach 😏A 2-hour drive from Chania crossing the Topolia gorges (magnificent winding road, I do not validate some opinions...), we discover the business of this “protected” natural site.Arriving at 10:30 a.m., the parking lots are already full 😓… The tourist bus stop is located right in front of a small supermarket which fills up with people at high speed, it puts you in the mood….! You are already struggling to buy a simple bottle of water!What can we say about the beach…. 😱 very pretty of course but ruined by mass tourism.People are literally stuck together on the sandbanks.It is therefore normal that the famous pink sand is now so rare…Be careful of the harsh sun... no shaded corners... you cook very quickly! It is also almost impossible to use a parasol because the site is very windy.Escape the overcrowded main beach, head to the left where you will find several small coves to isolate yourself but be careful, the tranquility is only short-lived!We left at 1 p.m., it was becoming unbearable...😭We preferred Balos but we have bitter memories of these 2 superb sites which have been badly deteriorated. It would be urgent to establish at least visitor quotas!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Super nice and cozy - can definitely be recommended!!! Possibility to park nearby for 5eur and several places nearby if you can buy food and drinks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So what can I say. Shared between the fact that the site is magnificent, but that it is completely ruined by the amount of people found there. It has become a tourist trap with its parking lots for €5, its deckchairs for €20 per day, its toilets for €1 and the various merchants, each as unpleasant as the next.The water is transparent and warm. For the pink sand.... thank you photoshop. In short I wanted to give a rating of 5/5 for the place but it will be 2 max.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Idyllic in book photos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a view and a paddle with hundreds or even more of other people. If you love being very close and personal with other people this is for you, drone flyers paradise to invade your privacy, and a square metre of sand to relax. We felt it was just too overcrowded, queues to get there, queues to get to the beach, 500 metre walk, and queue to pay your 5eur car park fee. The photos of empty beaches and idyllic scenery are best seen in books....in short an experience...not in my itinerary to do again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A special place worth seeing.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I read the last review from Pamela I think from Patonga Aust and wondered whether I should go or not. I am so glad I did not let that review put me off. This is a special place. Yes the drive there was at times hair raising but boy when isn’t it in the Greek islands. The place was thronging with people and we ignored the first couple of parking lots and kept driving until we could go no further and there is abuse parking lot there. They charge 5€ for the day, 300 metre walk to the beach. I agree it’s crowded and so my advice would be go very early but despite the crowds we had a great time. The place is picturesque with an amazing back drop. On the way back drop into one of the many small tavernas in the small mountain villages.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pink beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Without a doubt, the most beautiful beach I have ever been to. Of course, there can be a lot of people, but even that doesn't bother us. 2013.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turquoise sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very pleasant lagoon with sand, the sea is clear and turquoise. It is very hot with little shade, it is better to go there early in the morning before the arrival of tourists like us! Paid parking but don't let the first guard influence you to park closer to the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Everything is possible, nothing is neccesary.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach, certainly one of the most beautiful in Crete, but unfortunately difficult to get to and very crowded with tourists. The journey from Chania was cheap. €29 per person for a guided trip and return (the price with public transport is €20). Unfortunately, we only stayed for 3.5 hours but spent 2.5 hours each way there and back (54 km each way). We can say "we saw it", but we wouldn't have to make the journey again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nice place for walk around the isle, and shalow and clear water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: nice beach, perfect for a morning walk around the island.nice and clear water, recomended to stay until 11.00, maximum 12.00, when it willbe too crowdedmust arrive until 9, because are just few sunbedspink sand? just a joke, and marketing 😉

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magnificent site
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always the same, try to get there early in the morning to avoid the crowds.This site is exceptional and unique of its kind.The pink sand is not present everywhere and is not eye-catching but this place remains magnificent 😀

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but too many people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: At ten in the morning the umbrellas of the first establishment you come across were already finished! Then from 11am hundreds of people started arriving (even buses for groups) and the beach became unlivable... the water is obviously very beautiful and always very shallow, warm and the place is immense, there are many small beaches that you come to create between one rock and another and make the experience curious. Instead the pink sand is no longer there because tourists have taken it away over the years and now it is imperceptible, if you have seen it pink on Google it is only thanks to photoshop! With fewer people it would have been a different experience, which is a shame because it is a truly beautiful and special place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enchanting beach with intense light blue water, very fine pink sand, the only drawback is the road to get from Kissamos which is tortuous and at times with overhangs

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't go there! It's not like it used to be!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's terrible what has happened to this beautiful beach. We were there in 2022 and 2021. It was full, you had to be there early in the morning. Everything was fine for once. But this year everything is different! Parking spaces far above the beach, the fun costs €5. Then you walk towards the beach with what feels like thousands of other people. Then the big surprise. There are only 1/5 of the loungers and umbrellas left at most! At 10 a.m. everything was already taken. We saw many astonished faces. We then decided to leave this terrible place and went to Falassarna beach. Avoid at all costs!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too hard for anyone with disabilities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Far to far to walk for a person with disabilities … no transport to assist. Hardly any shelter.  Beautiful views but it should be made clear that it’s only for people who are able bodied.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Indecency once again in a natural environment!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Once again in another beautiful landscape of our country, money, rudeness and the plug, excel!Parking with a fee of 5 euros with the way I want (while there is a free space next to the beach) because someone likes it that way.Charge from the canteen to go (listen, listen) to the toilet!The need became chargeable. As for the employees, let's not argue, they were the rudest I've ever met.Shame on the rest of the Cretans for the defamation!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What pink sand?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After an 1/12 hour death defying drive from Chania we discovered that you had to use a fee charging, over crowded parking area and then walk at least a kilometre from the car to the beach.  The beach was also crowded with tourists from the buses.  We rested at a restaurant overlooking the beach for a mediocre lunch.  From there we observed the beach and the people and decided it wasn’t worth the effort.Perhaps it was because it was midday arriving that there was no visible pink sand?  Realised it was a tourist trap, decided not to stay and prayed we got home again!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely not a must!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First of all, the beach is really beautiful, but unfortunately you can't enjoy it at all. In the morning it's still OK but around midday there are crowds of people that you can't imagine and there were more and more of them. We had positioned ourselves at the edge and when we came out of the water we could hardly get to our towels because we were surrounded by others, only a few centimeters away. Most people were lying in the sun the whole time in temperatures of over 30 degrees, they're sure to have fun the next day. Then we walked back to the car and saw the extent of it when all the parking lots and the street were full, plus there were at least 8 tour buses, you'd think you were at an exhibition center. You can definitely save yourself the trouble, we've been to beaches that were at least as beautiful and that you could enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views were amazing and being in a pink sand beach was breathtaking. We went early morning so we had the beach just for ourselves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Death roads on Crete
reviewsWithKeywords.text: ROAD NOT AS IT SEEMS - Be very careful, if taking a trip from Elafonissi  to Paleochora the sat nav will give you 3 routes… do NOT TAKE THE SHORTEST ROUTE !! This route starts off okay with a decent tarmac road and barriers, but after about 8 km when you’re on top of the mountain through the tunnel and along a bit -  it turns into a gravel TRACK only fit for donkeys - you are so far up and there’s nowhere to turn around, there are no barriers and the drops are absolutely white, knuckling horrendous!!  for some reason Google Waze, and other Sat nav’s will give you this route as a good road - but it is not- , people will die here - this is not a joke - please take a paper map  so you can see these roads are completely uncompleted and are absolutely terrifying, anyone in a small car will not make it and if you think you’re going to take an hour like the sat nav advises think again - it’ll take you over three hours terrifying cliff edges and rocks falling down along the way. The cliffs absolutely so dangerous- do not go this route.  turn back as soon as you see gravel dirt road after tarmac and go the longer route !!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pure magic!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What can you say about this beach!Just take a look at photos, imagine that when you are there it is even more beautiful and you will get an idea.. My advice: visit it as early as you can so that it is less crowded, because as the time goes by it gets suffocatingly full, take a hat and a strong sunscreen (there aren't many shady areas) and ideally, closed shoes as it takes a bit of walking to get there. Drinks and snacks can also be found near the car park.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excursions
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Magnificent beaches, the sand is very pink. We had a good swimThe sun was shining. We found a place where we were alone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonissi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very nice beach on the south side of the island . Like all Greek islands , you should always check the wind speed and direction before heading out to a beach . If its windy from the north direction, go to the south beaches and vice versa. I agree with others who say that it gets really busy and getting an umbrella and lounges may be a problem . The water is crystal clear and remains shallow quite far out . Interestingly though , I kept feeling myself getting bit on my legs by tiny fish . Like others have also said , we found little to no pink sand . Nonetheless, you should visit while in Crete.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning but busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is quite rightly listed as one of the best beaches in the world. It is stunning and in certain locations it is also pink which is very beautiful.However as you would expect with such a beautiful beach it gets very busy and unless you get there early you are unlikely to get anywhere with shade. The water is crystal clear and shallow so ideal for children.One other thing to note is that you can not park that close to the beach so there is quite a walk to the beach which is up hill on the way back.Would recommend that you visit but be prepared for the crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nugget
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Indeed, parking lots are chargeable, 5th mid-September. We parked further up the road but be careful we arrived early because otherwise you will have to walk.From the last parking lot, 10/15 min walk downhill with stones, and then you will have to find a place on the sand. I saw a water pull-out for disabled people but I will admit that I wondered how they managed to get down to the beach from the public parking lot. Perhaps the nearest parking lot, currently closed to most people, is accessible to them.The good news is that the site is huge, in mid-September there were a lot of people but not overcrowded.The advantage of this beach compared to Balos is snorkeling. In Balos there is not much in the lagoon, you will have to dive into the deep blue where the strong winds cool the water temperature. Here too the wind can blow but there is excitement under the water even at the edge. Especially sars who will be delighted to enjoy your few picnic crumbs. Moving towards the rocks, you won't know where to look under the turquoise waters.You directly see the pink on the sand at the water's edge. It's not neon like some filter-loving Instagrammers would like you to believe, but the pink is there and it's beautiful, really. We actually shook our towels well when we left to leave these little shells and stones where they were born!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely- as per everyone's photo's
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went as part of a coach tour (good luck if you drive on these roads not wide enough for two vehicles to pass). The pink sand was a few inches as the tide comes in . Beautiful place nonetheless. Sea seemed a mixture of turquoise,blue and green.safe and sandy.5 euros to park all day.few eating places and mini markets before you go down on to the beach. Definitely worth the effort.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing development, although the beach was great until now
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely disappointing development! We were there in June and September 2022 and really enjoyed the time - you could drive close to the beach, for free, had plenty of space, enough loungers and umbrellas at an OK price - a lot of people, but absolutely OK and everything was well distributed.Since mid-2023, the area has been converted into a "nature reserve" which really doesn't deserve its name! Since the parking spaces are now much further up and are now subject to a fee, all the crowds of people just walk all over the so-called protected area and leave plastic behind like everywhere else and trample everything down - hardly in the spirit of nature conservation! Only a small part of the beach has loungers and umbrellas, you can't "just" rent loungers for further back, it's unbearable without an umbrella - which means that people even put their beach towels in the shade in the cordoned off areas - counterproductive if you want to preserve nature!!We are extremely disappointed that it is now just a money-making scheme - we would have happily paid for the parking space further down the road a year ago if it hadn't been so run down. I hope those responsible will take another look at this extremely questionable concept.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A highlight of our Crete holiday this year
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We thought long and hard about whether we should take the two-hour trip to the beach with a small child and ultimately decided to do it. We were not disappointed. Yes, it is all very touristy, but the view of the beach makes up for everything. Simply fantastic. We were also lucky enough to be there early enough to get one of the few loungers with a parasol. For us, it was a highlight of this year's Crete holiday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was probably not pink as the advertisements say, but we had a really nice day, the water is completely crystal clear and the sandy bottom is just lovely. It was worth the whole drive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Influencer catastrophe
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Completely overrated. Was there 15 years ago in September, you could drive to the beach, there were no loungers, etc. and you had the island to yourself. Currently you can see how certain influencers are ruining all the insider tips. In mid-September 2023, it feels like thousands of people are there, parking spaces are full and rip-offs from the parking lot to the lounger. When there are even tour buses in the parking lot, you know it's better to turn around. I'm glad I saw Elafonissi earlier without this madness. The same goes for Balos and Falassarna.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded, but…
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When it is crowded, it’s not nearly the experience one thinks they’re going to get from the pics. By early afternoon (it was a 2 hr drive!) every umbrella and lounger is taken and you are relegated to the hard, wet sand exposed by the tides.Within an hour of arrival, the winds started picking up and things (not just ours!) were blowing away!The water really is turquoise and beautiful, but that’s because it’s about 3 feet deep with a sandy bottom in the cove. Of course, with such a well-known, beautiful location, one shouldn’t expect to have it to oneself, but we were surprised at just how busy it was for mid-Sept.Be prepared to walk at least 1km downhill to the beach area (and uphill on the way back) from the multiple car parks up the hill from the beach, where you will pay 5€ to park on a flattened rocky area.I would imagine it COULD feel like paradise very early or late in the day, when you may have the views and beach to yourself, but outside LC that, it felt very much like a “check the box” experience on the very southwestern edge of Crete.The drive TO the beach from the east takes one through some very rugged and narrow terrain, although the raid quality itself was quite decent. Be prepared to stop on some corners, as two cars are one too many in certain locations! Driving through the tunnel was cool though and I’ve no idea how the tour buses manage the drive?!I certainly don’t want to leave a negative impression, because I’m sure we could have had a very different experience if our trip had been a little more planned or thought out, but just be prepared to wonder both where the pink sand is and how on earth most of the empty beach pictures were taken!All in all, definitely a meh day out for us, given it was a 4 hr round trip drive to visit.Take-always: Get there early. Buy shade. Take frequent dips. Try to stay out of the way of all the “soon-to-be Insta-Famous” 20-somethings. Bring suitable footwear for a somewhat steep and rocky 1Km+ walk to and from your parking spot.(If you are Disabled and have the permit, I believe you can drive down to the beach!)ENJOY! Caveat emptor.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Liefonissi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Like many, Elafonissi was sold to us as “the most beautiful beach on the ridge”, but paradise is only in name and then some.Firstly, the road is very, very long! We traveled 2 hours 40 minutes to get there, praying all you want to get there alive. The path is of unprecedented ignominy: steep path, narrow road, car rushing like madmen in front… in short, a nightmare as winding as it is endless. Don't worry, the rental car poses no risk, unlike your increased stress during the trip.Then, we “Park” you in a location that obviously costs €5 and then you have to walk down for about 15 minutes (the journey is not difficult and that’s the only thing)We arrived early and yet there was already a slew of tourists, as if the entire ridge had arranged to meet up that day (during the week)No deckchair available but at 20€ the sunbathing next to it is legal theft.Provide protection, parasols etc. because there is no shade and believe me it will cook like a cake in the oven.Let's talk about the beach now, certainly not everything is to be thrown away, the water is fresh and it feels good and translucent yes but it is in no way a paradise beach for me... but rather a shell in which to soak the feet. For that you have to go to Chrisi, Balos, Kedrodasos which is a few minutes away and much more sumptuous!In short, let's not even talk about pink which is non-existent, especially don't expect the Barbie pink that they sell you on the internet photos and postcards well Photoshopped for the occasion. There is a slight reflection but it doesn't break a duck's 3 legs and it's not worth driving so much for that.Unspoiled beach which is not that much... a lot of dirty places, it is forbidden to take "pink" sand at home, many do it so afterwards we should not be surprised that it eventually does not or more pink.There you go, very disappointed, having the feeling of having wasted my time to see a debacle of tourists, each more noisy and disrespectful than the other. Not at all relaxing!!To flee ! First category tourist trap.Ps: don't even think about dodging the parking payment, we'll kindly wait for you with the CB reader at the exit ;)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We are not in Riccione
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, certainly a destination for many and therefore quite crowded but if you adapt a little you can find a quiet space.As for the color, well, I didn't expect a pink beach from top to bottom (obviously) but even in this case if you move away from the masses and walk in the more isolated areas the sand on the shore is pink!Another fact that no one cares about: In my opinion, to be able to enjoy a holiday in places like Crete you need a bit of an adventurous spirit, a desire to walk (15 minute drive to reach the beach) and above all it is It is necessary to keep in mind that we are not in Riccione!That said, I highly recommend this beach!(P.s. even my grandmother could have done it on foot)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A paradise!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful place in Crete, after 26 years we returned and apart from the umbrellas and deckchairs and the kiosk it has fortunately remained unchanged, lots of people but in any case if you arrive early you can enjoy its charm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably the most beautiful beach in Crete and not only absolutely worth seeing with all the ingredients for a day to remember even if a little out of the way but a few more kilometers does not detract from the beauty of this beachSince the last time two years ago I have found some news they have made large paid parking lots about 1km before arriving at the beach they have removed all the umbrellas that were on the strip of sand that connects the various islets and they have increased the prices €20 per an umbrella and two sunbeds

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is magnificent!The lagoon is turquoise. Ideal in the off-season and don't hesitate to go a little further away from the beach to be even more peaceful!We were staying at the hotel next to the car park, so it was ideal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most amazing world class Greek beach.  Worth a visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go early! We arrived around 8:30 AM and left around 1 PM. The parking lot is a bit of a walk from the beach. The beach is amazing for swimming and walking to the other side of rock formations. The sand at the water's edge is pink from seashells. The water is crystal clear and very shallow for a ways from the edge.  We took many beautiful photos.  Bring towels, water, and lunch.  There are paid bathrooms (which is a shame.)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Never again
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It will also be the most beautiful beach in Crete or one of the most beautiful, go there if you love being overwhelmed by the crazy crowd. And even if you find yourself in a cot you won't even have space to turn around and for what then? the much photographed pink is now reduced to almost nothing, water certainly clear and beautiful as in many of our Sardinian beaches... nothing more!The sea of Greece is the Mediterranean emerald or sapphire, deep clean.. blue!I went there (and also early in the morning) I left the car in the car park, I walked and reached the beach I looked at it... or rather I tried to look at it by slaloming between the heads and I immediately went backIn Crete there is much, much better

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but gets extremely crowded.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is really beautiful, but before the crowds arrive (of course, everyone wants to see this beach, we were among them). We were there at a quarter to 9 (we set off at 5 a.m.). There were only 4 loungers occupied, so we still had the best choice. It is advisable to get a lounger in the front row, as you get the sun there all day (if you want, otherwise there are parasols everywhere) and no one can lie in front of you. The view from there is really beautiful. After we arrived, we were able to take pictures in peace and there was nothing to see in the background except the sea. Around 11 it gets really busy, you look around regularly and can't believe how many people are there at once. There is also a lot going on in the water afterwards.The pink in the water looks pretty, but not "to fall to your knees", perhaps there are days when this seems more intense. The water is really crystal clear and you can go very far into the water, so people are spread out relatively well.Parking costs €5 (I think that's too expensive) and two loungers + parasol €20 (I think that's OK), but I think the toilet use for €1 each is outrageous, especially because the toilets are pretty "filthy" and don't get any cleaner over the course of the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Still as beautiful but...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For reasons apparently of nature protection, parking has become paid and much further back from the beach (5€)!Why not if it's for a good cause, except that you shouldn't hesitate to go to the lowest parking lot and not be fooled by the callers who push you to park as soon as you arrive at the top, even if it means retrace your steps if indeed it is complete.Pay them by credit card, it's much safer....for nature 😉Sanitary facilities 1€ (and yes, nature must be preserved)A word of advice: It is better to be there at 10 a.m. if you want to get a parking space not very far away and a deckchair (20€/2) because places have become rare.What made this island strong was the kindness and smile of its inhabitants, the ease of everything. That was before... 4th and last stay for me 🥲

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Commercialization has now reached Greek beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the beach for the first time 2 years ago and were absolutely delighted. The parking spaces were close to the beach and free of charge, and the beach was equipped with loungers and parasols in such a way that you could still book loungers at 10 a.m. for a reasonable price. This year was completely different: you were no longer allowed to drive into the old parking spaces, but a large number of new parking spaces had been created above the beach, for which you had to pay €5. The loungers and parasols were equipped in such a way that you could no longer get anything by 9:30 a.m., which you only noticed after walking from the parking lot to the beach. In addition, 3 loungers and an umbrella cost €25. We then started our way home, but noticed that the most important item in the shops above the beach was an extremely large number of parasols. They were bought in abundance. As Greeks told us, this phenomenon has been observed since this year, after large parts of the area above the beach were apparently sold at the end of last year. What is happening here is what is now being reversed in other southern countries, namely commercialization at any price. We hope that many tourists will decide, as we did and will continue to do when visiting Crete, to avoid this beach despite its beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Meh
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived at this beach attracted by the idea of seeing the pink sand, but once we got there the pink color could barely be seen, the beach is certainly beautiful, very wide and with crystal clear water but the main reason why we went there it was actually the sand, which unfortunately left us with a bit of a bad taste in our mouths

reviewsWithKeywords.title: PA-RA-DI-SI-A-CA
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A magical place, with two types of sea: on one side swimming pool water with views reminiscent of La Maddalena, the other side with Caribbean colours, all framed by a wonderful pink sand which makes it, as a sea not as a view, more beautiful from Balos.It's all a free beach, you only pay 5 euros for parking and on the way back, after a tiring ascent, the market offers water for just 50 cents.After Cayo Largo, the most beautiful sea I've seen in my life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: exceptional
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spectacular beach with water so crystal clear that you can safely drink breathtaking colors, umbrellas and sunbeds for the price of €20, 5 meters from the water, top of the top of the island of Crete, an experience that I will never forget in my exceptional life

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Delicious crest, where are you?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach indeed very beautiful but let's look around. First of all, 6 years ago, we left the cars in a large parking lot adjacent to the beach, today it is paid parking, 5€, and stations of the cross to reach the sea, no path, everyone passes anywhere, scrap metal on the ground, trampled vegetation, remains of cement.... So we logically wonder where the parking money goes? To the municipality? Local mafia? No ticket here, just a kidam who jumps on you to get the money and believe me, there is something to do, no definitely, it is no longer the ridge that we loved so much, now we see the tourist coming from very, very far away and it's who will gorge themselves the most. For us, the ridge is over. And be careful, the beaches are covered with parasols and deckchairs, obviously paying. Example of a beach in Bali where you can no longer see the sand and it’s only just beginning!!!! 😢

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the best on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach seems overrated. It is wicked windy, barely any pink sand and it’s crowded. I much preferred balos and Gramvousa island over here. Also have to pay for parking and then it’s about a 15 minute walk to the beach and good luck finding a spot. They should also try to get more chairs and umbrellas because im sure more people would pay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful but...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: unsurprisingly, the beach is crowded even when arriving early in the morning. very beautiful beach all the same. It's quite windy, bring a parasol because places near rocks or shrubs are expensive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but at what price?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a hard time, there were a lot of people, it was impossible to park despite the touts asking us to join their parking lots. Then we had to walk 10 minutes to reach the beach, there were gusts of wind, we were getting sand and dust everywhere. On the beach it was even more exposed. We got so much sand in our faces that we had to leave after 20 minutes. Make sure there is no wind at all before going. In the end, 1h30 drive for 20 minutes of beach eating sand and 5 euros for parking. Ugh

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better to go to another beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were terribly disappointed. The way there was adventurous but doable on good roads, but the way back was pure hell. No solid roads up or down. We set off extra early to avoid the rush, which worked out really well, but it was slightly cloudy and what pink sand was left was barely noticeable. Not recommended at all.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful lagoon. On the other hand, don't expect to see pink sand (or maybe it depends on the time of day). Despite the crowds you can find tranquility if you go opposite. We had a little cove all to ourselves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful place. Go there early in the morning, to avoid the crowds with the excursions (arrive around 11:30). There is something to eat nearby, it is possible to rent deckchairs on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maybe a little overrated place.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is nice and swimmable yes, but car parking area very far of the beach ,uphill walk over a 1km...If you want to rent a sunbed, you must be there very early. 9am is too late, then all beds are sold out already...And the amount of people..... 5000-7000 visitors every day and only 200 sunbeds... Still we enjoyed our stay there for a day in extreme heat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Natural swimming pool or sea?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches we visited this year in Crete. Definitely on the podium, equal with Balos. It feels like being in natural pools: shallow, crystalline water and fine white sand. Lido umbrella + 2 sunbeds = €20The only flaw is that the beach stations are too close to each other

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most amazing beaches I’ve ever seen in my life.  It was hard to get to but totally worth it!!!  Perfect water perfect sand.  Thank you universe :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't waste your time...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go on your way, long journey to get there, the photos you see do not reflect reality. Too many people in the afternoon on September 6 (impossible to go there in the morning because it rained that day), color of the water certainly beautiful but beach with wet sand, towel soaked instantly before even going into the water . Parking 5€ per day, by touts while the place is not private, you can go higher without paying. Don't expect to park near the water as you can see on GoogleMaps, this parking lot is closed you have to walk (besides everyone tramples the vegetation hoping to find the shortest path, nature doesn't tell you no thanks...). In short there are other beaches more beautiful and more relaxing than here, most come to take photos, no interest in rest. Place for tourists, not for travelers ;)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crystal clear water and pink sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach, a little crowded.Equipped with umbrellas for €20, I recommend not arriving after 10.00 because they end quickly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular play
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spectacular beach... From the level of Balos beach. But much bigger. Crystal clear water, lagoon...a paradise...the downside is the road to get there and the crowds of people...but since the beach is large it is perfect. Parking costs 5 euros and you walk 5 minutes from the parking lot because they don't allow car access to the beach... fortunately...It is a beach that is windy...but not in an exaggerated way... It has bathrooms and some snack bars. Ice cream....on the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely worth seeing!! There are several car parks (4) costing €5 for the whole day. There is a bit of walking downhill on a dirt road, 5 minutes but the view is guaranteed! There are 3 mini establishments with umbrellas, walkways, bathrooms, showers also for people with disabilities. If you can't find an umbrella, there are trees on the sides (both right and left) to find some shade. The roads to reach this beach, by Greek standards, are excellent: I started from Paleochora, some were recently asphalted.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clay in the heart
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, with a thousand colours, very suggestive. There is a bar just after the path to drink and eat... we were 2 families with children and the only flaw is that there is little shade and few umbrellas but absolutely worth seeing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Elafonisi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I will start with caveats don’t stop at first car park they r trying to get you drive on as there is another car park closer. It’s 10 min from there to beach b prepared to pay £20 for two deckchairs cash or card there are enough cafes for food and drink . Water is clear and sand is pink on edges check the weather as we went when windy but it is lovely and shallow (doesn’t suit everyone but safer for younglings ) just walk out further

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A holiday in Crete alone is worth it..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach, difficult to identify the contours that protrude and fall following the shape of the many small bays that compose it. The context is that of a natural oasis, therefore being able to observe the typical dunes, the rocks protruding from the sometimes pink sand and the semi-desert vegetation with plants and flowers. One of the most beautiful beaches ever seen, perhaps the most beautiful. It's true, lots of people but the effect of the crowding thins out as you push towards the end of the route, a few extra steps rewarded by the hidden beauty of the more distant bays.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Depends!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It depends where you're from! The sea is clear and the surrounding landscape is particular, made up of mountains and red earth. Very nice but a little overrated. For those accustomed to the beautiful sea this is not all a surprise. However, the pink sand and the always shallow water are particular. This is why it is recommended for children.Beach equipped with only a few umbrellas, so you have to arrive in the early hours of the morning but it depends on the day..Then pay attention to the journey to get there... Road with sheer mountain bends, buses pass almost miraculously! However, the view is very beautiful, truly breathtaking, but for those who suffer from vertigo there is a good half hour of fear 😅Despite everything recommended!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful lagoon but a lot to do for the environment
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The lagoon is still beautiful, however it is regrettable that paths are not made to go to the beach, everyone walks anywhere on the vegetationConsidering the price of parking, I think that this income could be used to improve the surroundings of the beach and create paths.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday at the end of August
reviewsWithKeywords.text: In my opinion it is overrated.Very crowded, with few umbrellas that do not satisfy the needs of the thousands of people who are there...And then the pink beach?? ....we didn't see it....Crete is all beautiful, but in my opinion there are other beaches in the south of the island (e.g. SKINARIA, in my opinion the best ever) which are less known but which are worth visiting as they have nothing to envy of Elafonissi or to the famous balos lagoon...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous sea. I won't add anything else to what has already been written in other reviews except that in September the water is particularly cold. Maybe better in other periods.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A paradise!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is absolutely heaven on earth, truly beautiful!Shallow water at first calm and crystal clear! Possibility to do water sports, my husband did kitesurfing!Umbrella and 2 sunbeds for €20 all day, which considering the place is quite a bit!However, you have to come early in the morning because then people start to arrive and you risk not finding a place, there is also a lot of free beach space that you can use.There's a spit of land that you can cross and go to a really gorgeous little island!The beach is equipped with everything: bars, bathrooms, showers! I highly recommend it because it's worth it!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely yes, but definitely worth it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You have to agree with the previous comments. It is very, very crowded and very overcrowded. Lots of tourists come and go. Not necessarily suitable for relaxing.BUT:The beach makes up for everything. The water is a wonderful blue. The beach is slightly pink as described. Sometimes more, sometimes less. You can dive wonderfully and look for fish. There is something to eat and drink and the day is saved. The journey there is just as beautiful and eventful. It is definitely worth it, as the large crowds of people also disperse.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dream beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful beach which is worth the detour but don't expect to see pink sand!There are a few here and there but it's not as rosy as on the Internet!But still very niceTo do

reviewsWithKeywords.title: UNMISSABLE
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Elafonissi is certainly on the podium of the most beautiful beaches in Crete, nothing to say, it deserves it!I recommend arriving VERY early especially in the peak months, as it fills up very quickly, if you want to enjoy it without many people and walk on every side of this beautiful beach you have to be there by 9 in the morning.Possibility of renting umbrellas and sunbeds at a cost of 20 euros, but arrive very early for these too, they sell like hot cakes!Possibility of a free beach, there are some bars, which offer salads, clubs, sandwiches, ice creams, drinks.The closest car park is the first one, i.e. the last one you find when arriving by car costs 5 euros, from there you will then have to walk and reach the beach, it is a stony stretch but mostly flat, it is not very tiring, if you have the better shoes.The sand is pink and is enchanting reflected in its crystal clear waters.Arrive early and then leave around 3pm at the latest, as especially on Sundays crowds of people will arrive, and the beach will lose its real beauty.Elafonissi has a special place in my heart.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A corner of paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is truly a beautiful beach, an expanse of water and shades, a corner of paradise. A long way to reach it but when you are there Roman enchanted.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pity.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic site spoiled by the cult of money. They cut off the access of vehicles (after the asphalt road) and they "have" a parking space for you, right before (essentially they oblige you because the first free space is 1km before) for 5€ all day. The sunbeds, the set €20(!!!).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I, who am not a beach person, had difficulty leaving this place, simply extraordinarily beautiful!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Another superb beach in the Chania region, easier to access than Balos and the same colors the site is perhaps larger than Balosbring water and a picnic to have a good time (downstairs there is something to eat, the prices are reasonable but I didn't find it terrible).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tourist trap
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Winding road but largely doable to get into the clutches of the parking lot touts (5€).11 a.m. hundreds of people head towards the beach, it loses all its charm.We went there one day when the wind was blowing quite strongly.. the deckchairs were taken over and the sand was wet. Soaked towels before even sitting down.We left for Aspri Limni Beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It’s very beautiful. It’s very fine. The sand is certainly not as pink as in the advertisement. From the parking lot it’s a good 15 minutes walk, you need to have a comfortable
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everything is beautiful. Only a lot of buses and private cars and crowds of people arrive at once. There is no place to lie down. The parking lot is far from the beach. It’s very beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not easily accessible
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach but not easily accessible,  from car park there is a downhill walk and the walk back up, not recommended for those with mobility issues

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely worth visiting. For those who aren't early risers like us, the advice is to go for a swim after 5pm, when the crowds begin to thin out and you can find parking in the space closest to the entrance (5 euros). The walk to the beach takes only 10 minutes (timed), which at that time is very doable without getting too hot.There is very little pink left, but the place is a true paradise. A mandatory stop for anyone visiting Crete.
